targets.name: caveman
targets.head: bad48a0e1df55e05e3f52249afa35ecc1909ee76
targets.scope_notes: agent-tool profile: a token-compression engine, CLI, proxy and MCP server that agents call; uses_crypto true (SigV4, OIDC JWT, TLS, AES) and parses_untrusted true (compresses tool/web payloads); has_ui false (CLI/engine, no GUI); heavy_compute false.

gaps.title: Single-maintainer project with no governance
gaps.case: README.md:318 states 'One person maintains this for free'; there is no CODEOWNERS or governance doc (meta.codeowners/meta.governance), only CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, across a six-product polyglot monorepo installed widely.
gaps.impact: sustainability / supply chain: bus-factor and continuity risk for a CLI with a very large install base.
gaps.fix: Add CODEOWNERS, recruit a second maintainer and publish a governance/succession process.

gaps.title: Static analysis is uneven across the largest languages
gaps.case: CI runs only tsc --noEmit (TS types) and go vet (packages/cli/package.json:32, engine-ci.yml:29); there is no golangci-lint/staticcheck, no gofmt gate, no ESLint and no Python linter or type checker, over 93k lines of Go, 41k TS and 22k Py.
gaps.impact: maintainability: the cheapest defect filter is applied inconsistently to the bulk of the code.
gaps.fix: Add golangci-lint + gofmt gate, ruff + mypy for Python and ESLint for TS to CI.

gaps.title: Large undocumented configuration surface
gaps.case: The probe reads 255 environment variables of which only ~108 appear in docs (obs.env_vars), and there is no single validated config schema.
gaps.impact: operability: operators of the proxy/runtime face hidden settings and no schema to validate against.
gaps.fix: Document and validate every environment variable at startup and publish a config schema.

gaps.title: Flagship session number not reproducible at this commit
gaps.case: The headline '33.2% fewer input tokens' session result is, per docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md, an August-2026 older-engine run with no committed raw pairs (benchmarks/results/.gitkeep), and the evals snapshot is n=10 single-run.
gaps.impact: epistemic/reproducibility: the flagship number cannot be reproduced on the shipped engine (the doc discloses this, which lowers severity).
gaps.fix: Commit raw session pairs and re-run the session benchmark on the current engine, dated.

gaps.title: Cryptography has no inventory, abstraction or PQC plan
gaps.case: The gateway uses TLS, OIDC JWT (RS256/ES256), AWS SigV4 and AES directly (proxy/internal/identity, shared/platform/awssig) with no algorithm inventory, replaceable layer or post-quantum plan.
gaps.impact: horizon/compliance: CNSA 2.0 and the NIST 2030-35 transition are unprepared for the gateway's signing/TLS.
gaps.fix: Document a crypto inventory, route crypto through one abstraction and publish a dated ML-KEM/ML-DSA plan.

gaps.title: Mirrored source trees can drift
gaps.case: skills/ is mirrored into plugins/caveman/skills, browse/ is a declared consumer copy of another repo, and the Apache text is repeated across many directories (~86 duplicate files per the cross-repo dissection).
gaps.impact: maintainability: two copies of a skill or doc can diverge and an agent may read the stale one.
gaps.fix: Generate the mirrors at build time and assert byte-equality in CI, or single-source them.

gaps.title: SBOMs shipped but no VEX
gaps.case: Releases attach CycloneDX SBOMs (release-packages.yml:318) but emit no VEX statements for known CVEs (SEC-4).
gaps.impact: compliance: buyers cannot see which SBOM-listed CVEs are exploitable vs not-affected.
gaps.fix: Emit OpenVEX alongside each release SBOM.

opps.title: Extract the CCR recovery store as a standalone package
opps.description: The Context Recovery store (content-addressed sha256 handles, SQLite WAL, atomic/fail-closed, idempotent, byte-exact recovery) is a self-contained hub (dissection score 18). Extracted, it is a reusable recovery substrate for REA Evidence, Absurd steps and strix tool-output spill.

opps.title: Share one content-addressed retrieval handle with REA and strix
opps.description: caveman's CCR handle, REA's evidence_id and strix's tool-output spill are all content-addressed. A single retrieval-handle standard lets a compressed view, an evidence record and an agent tool result interoperate so summaries never lose the original.

opps.title: Publish the S0-S4 safety-class ladder as a transform-honesty standard
opps.description: The engine's S0-S4 registry (byte-safe vs model-visible, requires-CCR, reversible) plus the byte-safe passthrough contract is a reusable honesty standard any transform tool could declare against, composable with ponytail's necessity ladder as policy-as-code.

opps.title: Add VEX to become a CRA-complete reference for the set
opps.description: caveman already ships provenance, SBOMs, cosign signatures and OpenSSF Scorecard; adding OpenVEX closes the last gap and makes it a dated-obligation-ready supply-chain reference the other reviewed repos can copy.

opps.title: Consolidate token accounting into one measured budget library
opps.description: Offline token accounting (tiktoken o200k, honest-numbers method) is implemented here and conceptually duplicated in leanrea's context-budget, strix's context_budget and pi's compaction. One measured budget library would serve all of them.

reeng.component: CI static analysis across Go/TS/Python
reeng.gain: a uniform defect filter over the whole codebase
reeng.measure: golangci-lint + gofmt gate + ruff + mypy + ESLint run green in CI on every change

reeng.component: project governance and bus-factor (CODEOWNERS, maintainers)
reeng.gain: continuity for a widely-installed CLI
reeng.measure: CODEOWNERS committed, at least two active maintainers and a governance/succession doc published

reeng.component: engine/ccr recovery store
reeng.gain: a reusable content-addressed recovery substrate for the reviewed set
reeng.measure: a published package consumed by at least one other repo with a recovery round-trip parity test

reeng.component: configuration surface (environment variables)
reeng.gain: no hidden configuration for proxy/runtime operators
reeng.measure: every environment variable documented and validated at startup and a config schema published

targets.name: rea
targets.head: b4938aed58737293a6987630476632619713f5cd
targets.scope_notes: Profile agent-tool, not the suggested agent-harness: REA is an MCP server and CLI that agents call to inspect shipped artifacts (the standard names REA as its agent-tool example), and the harness suggestion came from 23 website HTML files; has_ui=false because those files are the docs website and one test fixture; uses_llm=true (run by agents, ships a skill and 6 prompts, calls no model); executes_code, parses_untrusted, network_service (opt-in HTTP), uses_crypto (HMAC bridge auth, OpenPGP checks) and distributed (npm, MCP Registry) are true; heavy_compute=false (single analyses reach about 1,000 s, no training or inference). Static evidence is from b4938ae; runtime evidence is from the earlier study of the published 6.7.0 package and is labelled as such.

gaps.title: Default MCP catalog costs about 833k tokens and results are sent twice
gaps.case: Default tools/list for 6.7.0 is 3,158,368 bytes (832,930 o200k tokens), and output schemas are 2,353,893 bytes of it (74.5%). At b4938ae both schema profiles still default to full (src/config/mcpInputSchemaProfile.ts:24; docs/mcp-contracts.md:959-962). Each result is returned as both text and structuredContent (docs/mcp-contracts.md:12-13). Traces copy all parent-graph limitations (src/domain/javascript/javascriptFeatureTrace.ts:151-154): a 3-node trace was 1,424,753 bytes, 98.8% of it limitations.
gaps.impact: Hosts that load tools eagerly pay the catalog on every request, and some reject it outright (issues #1484, #2512, #2813, #2999 cited in docs/mcp-contracts.md). Repeated payloads exhaust the response budget sooner and waste agent context.
gaps.fix: Make the measured compact input profile and omitted or lazily served output schemas the default; reference parent limitations by digest; return a short text pointer next to structuredContent; fail CI when tools/list bytes exceed a budget.

gaps.title: Large sessions cannot be re-imported and the largest results are unreachable over MCP
gaps.case: On 6.7.0, export_evidence_bundle wrote 889,074,095 bytes, and import_evidence_bundle failed after 107 s with 'Invalid string length' at 5.56 GB peak RSS. trace_application_feature and compare_application_versions exceeded a 64 MiB response budget (86.6 s and 153.2 s). b4938ae adds a streaming JSON reader (src/application/JsonInputFile.ts:256-280); whether it fixes this case was not verified.
gaps.impact: Complete results of large analyses (about 1,000 s each) cannot be consumed by an agent or carried to another connection, though they were computed.
gaps.fix: Use a record-streamed bundle format (JSONL) validated record by record; page traces and version comparisons; add a round-trip test at 10x the largest observed bundle.

gaps.title: The Evidence ledger is lost when the process dies
gaps.case: EvidenceLedger keeps records and unknowns in in-memory Maps (src/application/investigation/EvidenceLedger.ts:44-47). After SIGKILL the ledger fell from 3 records to 0; an Absurd-backed prototype restored all 6 Evidence IDs with 0 repeated calls (prototype-crash-test.json).
gaps.impact: A crash or client restart discards all analysis in the session and every retained reference, so long analyses (1,000 s, 6.3 GB worker) must be repeated.
gaps.fix: Append every Evidence record and unknown revision to a durable per-session log (JSONL or SQLite WAL) and replay it at start; add a CI kill-and-resume test that compares Evidence IDs with an uncrashed control.

gaps.title: Errors give wrong retry advice, hide causes and differ for the same mistake
gaps.case: invalid_request is always retryable (src/domain/analysisErrorProjection.ts:569-576), so a missing file returns retryable: true. A rejected unknown resolution ('no qualifying resolution evidence', src/domain/evidenceBundle.ts:409-412) is wrapped as an integrity error (src/application/investigation/EvidenceLedger.ts:436) and shown as 'Evidence state changed ... try again' (src/domain/analysisErrorPresentation.ts:274-275). A string-length limit on import surfaced as evidence_integrity_mismatch. The same wrong-format input returns invalid_request/retryable:true from inspect_pe_resources and capability_unavailable/retryable:false from inspect_managed_artifact; docs/installation.md:360-363 notes caller-dependent codes.
gaps.impact: Agents retry calls that cannot succeed or misdiagnose the cause, which wastes calls and context.
gaps.fix: Derive retryable from the failure cause; carry the validator reason in details.reason; map resource limits to resource_constraint; add a table-driven test that sends equivalent invalid inputs to sibling tools and asserts one code and retry flag.

gaps.title: REA cannot inventory its own distribution format, and no lane runs it on itself
gaps.case: 6.7.0 rejected its own npm .tgz ('unsupported binary format'), and open_binary refused the unpacked package directory (findings.jsonl E2-1; e2-e3-stages.json). At b4938ae the ZIP-family formats and Evidence subject formats include no tar or gzip format (src/domain/zipPackageFormat.ts:2-11; src/domain/evidence.ts:45-70). No CI lane analyzes the release tarball.
gaps.impact: npm packages, the main distribution form in REA's JavaScript target ecosystem, have to be repacked by hand, and self-application regressions go unnoticed.
gaps.fix: Add a tar/gzip reader with the same path, size and identity controls as the ZIP reader; add a release lane that inventories and analyzes the qualified tarball and diffs it against the previous release.

gaps.title: The JavaScript application graph misses modern Node loading forms
gaps.case: On REA's own 6.7.0 package, native_addon_bindings was 0 although the package loads rea-windows-x64.node through createRequire(...)(fileURLToPath(new URL(...))) (E3-4). The worker loaded through import.meta.resolve('#javascript-analysis-worker') had no incoming reference edge (E4-1). Bridges referenced through new URL(..., import.meta.url) matched no graph entity (E4-2). No import.meta.resolve handling exists in src/domain/javascript at b4938ae (rg).
gaps.impact: Reported relationships and counts are incomplete for packages that use subpath imports and URL-relative loading, and an agent can conclude that no native addon exists.
gaps.fix: Resolve the literal forms import.meta.resolve, new URL(literal, import.meta.url) and createRequire(new URL(...)) through package imports and exports maps; add fixtures for each form; report unresolved dynamic loads as unknown in summary counts.

gaps.title: Process comparison counts timing as behaviour
gaps.case: Terminal frames are compared together with at_ms (src/domain/process/processObservation.ts:10-14), and exit comparison includes settlement timing (src/domain/process/processComparison.ts:416-424; docs/process-capture.md:392-394). Two runs of a deterministic command with identical frames and exit codes 0/0 returned status changed (e8-process-compare.json).
gaps.impact: Behavioural diffs and reconstruction checks report changes that did not happen, so agents chase timing jitter.
gaps.fix: Compare content and ordering separately from timing; report timing as its own dimension with a stated tolerance; keep strict timing comparison as an explicit option.

gaps.title: No dependency updates, vulnerability or secret scanning, or SBOM
gaps.case: There is no Dependabot or Renovate configuration (probe deps.update_bot), no scanner in any of the 30 workflows (probe ci.security_scans) and no SBOM step (probe ci.sbom), for 40 runtime dependencies and 750 locked packages (package.json; package-lock.json).
gaps.impact: Known-vulnerable dependencies or committed credentials can ship unnoticed, and downstream users cannot answer SBOM requests.
gaps.fix: Add automated update PRs, an OSV or npm audit job, secret scanning, and a CycloneDX SBOM attached to each release next to the npm provenance.

gaps.title: The opt-in HTTP transport has no client authentication
gaps.case: rea mcp --http serves the full tool catalog over plain HTTP without client authentication (docs/mcp-contracts.md:459-463). Loopback binds check Host and Origin, but a non-loopback bind relaxes both with only a log warning (src/server/http/serveStreamableHttp.ts:98-108, 589-593). The Hopper and Ghidra bridges already use per-session capability tokens (SECURITY.md:27-32).
gaps.impact: Missing access control: on a shared host or an exposed bind, other users or network peers can invoke process-launching and device-changing tools with the REA user's privileges.
gaps.fix: Require a per-instance bearer token generated at startup, as the bridges do, and refuse non-loopback binds unless an explicit unsafe flag is given.

gaps.title: Breaking-change churn and maintainer concentration
gaps.case: There were 14 releases between 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-18, 9 with breaking changes; six breaking releases shipped as minors under always-bump-minor (CHANGELOG.md; docs/releasing.md:145-152), and 6.6.0 was tagged but never published (CHANGELOG.md:11). One maintainer authored 537 of 893 commits in 6.5.0 (docs/releases/6.5.0.contributions.json); there is no CODEOWNERS or governance file.
gaps.impact: Agents and pipelines that follow @latest (as README.md:107 shows) or caret ranges get breaking contract changes with no version signal, and continuity depends on one person.
gaps.fix: Use major versions for breaking changes, or publish a stable line with a declared support window; add CODEOWNERS and a short governance and succession note.

gaps.title: Injection resistance is untested and read-only hints are rarely set
gaps.case: Untrusted-content framing is tested only for the marker's presence (tests/boundary/mcp/targetContentFramingMcp.test.ts:46-60), and no agent evaluation scenario puts directives in target content (src/evaluation/AgentEvaluationFixtures.ts). readOnlyHint is true for 5 of 207 tools; 81 of 208 tools are non-read-only only because they record Evidence in REA's own in-memory session (src/contracts/toolEffects.ts).
gaps.impact: Prompt-injection regressions go undetected, and hosts that auto-approve read-only tools must prompt for almost every call, which weakens human review of the 31 destructive tools.
gaps.fix: Add an adversarial corpus (strings, pseudocode and page text with embedded directives) to the agent evaluation and assert that no tool call follows them; set readOnlyHint for tools whose only effect is in-process session recording, since MCP defines it as not modifying the environment.

gaps.title: No regulatory position for a distributed package
gaps.case: No document mentions the EU CRA or the AI Act (probe meta.compliance); the support policy is latest-only (SECURITY.md:5); no SBOM is produced.
gaps.impact: CRA vulnerability reporting (from 11 Sep 2026) and its main obligations (from 11 Dec 2027) may apply, depending on how REA is distributed, and users cannot judge their own obligations.
gaps.fix: Publish a short compliance note on the project's role (open-source steward or manufacturer), support period, vulnerability handling and SBOM plan.

opps.title: Compact catalog by default, with output schemas on request
opps.description: REA already ships a compact input profile and an output-schema-off profile that cut the 6.7.0 catalog from 3,158,368 to 219,226 bytes (-93%) while the server keeps canonical validation. Making them the default, with full schemas available through binary_session or resources, removes most of the per-session catalog cost in every host.

opps.title: Publish the effect vocabulary and untrusted marker as host policy
opps.description: REA's per-tool effect audit (executesForeignCode, mutatesDevice, accessesNetwork and others) and the _meta.provenance.untrusted_content marker are machine-readable. Harnesses in the reviewed set (orca, t3code, pandacode, agent-sandbox-lockdown, which already gates writes and logs tool calls) could enforce rules such as approval for executesForeignCode after untrusted content was read. That moves AGT-1 and AGT-2 controls from prompt wording to policy.

opps.title: Durable Evidence ledger on absurd or pi durable steps
opps.description: Move EvidenceLedger from in-memory Maps to durable steps. The Absurd-backed prototype restored a SIGKILLed session with 0 repeated calls and the same 6 Evidence IDs, and REA's content-addressed IDs make replay idempotent by construction. absurd (Postgres) or pi durable fit hosted use; a local SQLite WAL log is the lighter option for desktops.

opps.title: Route cheap questions to direct tool calls
opps.description: For header, symbol and string questions, a REA CLI call costs 1.3-2.3 s and 2-3 KB, against 4-26 ms for objdump, nm or strings. leanrea's recipe answered the 7 self-analysis questions in 219 ms and 2.5 KB, and leanrea's own benchmark reports 38% less wall time and 35% lower cost than REA 6.5.0, at 74/75 against 75/75. A routing table in the skill, plus Evidence recording for raw tool output, keeps provenance while removing most of the cost of simple questions.

opps.title: Investigation-level coverage document modelled on strix
opps.description: REA declares coverage for each result but not for a whole investigation. strix writes a run-level coverage.json that separates unaccounted classes from tested-and-nothing-found and marks partial runs. Pairing that document with REA's unknown and obligation ledgers would reconcile the questions asked with the outcomes for whole investigations (the EPI-4 horizon).

opps.title: Extract the Evidence record and unknown ledger as a standalone format
opps.description: The Evidence schema (subject digest, provider version, analysis profile, parameters, confidence, authority, environment, coverage, links, content-addressed ID over RFC 8785 JSON) and the residual-unknown ledger do not depend on REA's providers. A versioned JSON Schema with a small library would let strix findings, leanrea answers and caveman measurements exchange citable observations.

opps.title: Calibrate confidence classes with the my-jev and laya method
opps.description: No one checks the observed, derived and inferred classes against outcomes. The agent-evaluation fixtures already grade closed claims against oracles (src/evaluation/KnownAnswerEvaluation.ts). Feeding those results into a per-class precision report with Wilson intervals, as the earlier study did with the my-jev and laya method (observed 9/9, derived 3/4, below a 10-claim floor), yields the EPI-2 horizon measurement.

opps.title: Drop the duplicate per-module runtime tree from the package
opps.description: The package ships rolldown bundles and the complete per-module tsc output that workers load by path (scripts/bundle-runtime.mjs:6-9; package.json files['dist']). On 6.7.0 that was 15.7 MB of bundles plus 10.2 MB in 1,505 module files, with 163 files (694 KB) statically unreachable. Bundling the worker entry points as well removes the duplicate tree.

reeng.component: MCP catalog advertisement (src/contracts/compactInputSchema.ts, src/config/mcpInputSchemaProfile.ts, src/config/mcpOutputSchemaProfile.ts)
reeng.gain: Default tools/list falls from 3,158,368 to about 219,226 bytes (-93%, measured on 6.7.0), with no change to server-side validation.
reeng.measure: tools/list bytes and o200k tokens recorded per release in CI against a failing budget; the existing host lanes (Kimi, Gemini, pi-web-ui) stay green.

reeng.component: EvidenceLedger (src/application/investigation/EvidenceLedger.ts) and bundle import and export (src/application/EvidenceBundleFiles.ts)
reeng.gain: No Evidence lost on crash, and bundles larger than the V8 string limit round-trip.
reeng.measure: A CI kill -9 test gives the same Evidence IDs and 0 repeated provider calls as an uncrashed control; a 2 GB synthetic bundle imports successfully.

reeng.component: Error projection (src/domain/analysisErrorProjection.ts, src/domain/analysisErrorPresentation.ts, src/application/investigation/EvidenceLedger.ts)
reeng.gain: Correct retryable flags, preserved causes, and one code for each equivalent mistake.
reeng.measure: A table-driven sibling-tool test over invalid path, missing file, wrong format and unqualified resolution asserts code, retryable and details.reason; retry counts in verify:agent reports go down.

reeng.component: Supply chain (.github/workflows, package.json)
reeng.gain: Coverage of known vulnerabilities, secrets and dependency updates, plus an SBOM for every release.
reeng.measure: OpenSSF Scorecard result; a CycloneDX SBOM attached to each release that matches package-lock.json; days from advisory to dependency bump.

reeng.component: Per-module dist tree in the npm package (scripts/bundle-runtime.mjs, package.json files)
reeng.gain: About 10 MB and 1,500 fewer files in the package (6.7.0 figures).
reeng.measure: npm pack --json size and file count in the release rehearsal against a budget; worker start-up tests still pass.

targets.name: pi-durable
targets.head: fdce48eb404ec014adaf2ac10a3a53bc6b1740c2
targets.scope_notes: Profile agent-harness instead of the suggested workflow-engine: the package calls itself 'A durable agent harness' (README.md:5), runs model turns through pi-ai, executes bash/powershell, file-edit and QuickJS code-mode tools (README.md:243-366), and the standard lists durable agent runtimes under agent-harness. Flags: uses_llm=true (generation and compaction call models through @earendil-works/pi-ai, package.json:148; the probe missed it because it looks for third-party LLM SDKs); executes_code=true (src/tools/bash.ts, src/env/node.ts); parses_untrusted=true (read decodes arbitrary workspace files and image headers, src/images/exif.ts, src/tools/image.ts; model and tool output enter the context); has_ui=false and network_service=false (library, no listener found); uses_crypto=false (sha256 for change detection, random UUIDs for temp files); distributed=true (npm @earendil-works/pi-durable). Repository files (^/...) apply: license, SECURITY.md, CI, lockfile, AGENTS.md.

gaps.title: Agent tool defaults grant broad agency
gaps.case: Every installed extension is selected by default (README.md:241); bash takes an optional timeout with no default (src/tools/bash.ts:12) and passes inheritEnv: true (src/tools/bash.ts:76), which copies the whole host process environment into the command (src/env/node.ts:273-277); the quickstart reads the provider key from the environment (README.md:57); nested tool calls have no depth limit (README.md:329); approval exists only as a host-written hook (README.md:233).
gaps.impact: Excessive agency and unbounded consumption (OWASP LLM06, LLM10): commands chosen by a manipulated model can read credentials from the environment and return them into the transcript and the provider request; runaway commands or recursive nested calls have no ceiling.
gaps.fix: Default the shell environment to an allowlist (PATH, HOME, locale) with explicit opt-in for more, add a default command timeout and nesting depth limit, ship an opt-in approval extension for write and exec tools, and document these defaults.

gaps.title: No cross-process exclusion on a storage
gaps.case: README.md:783 states 'One process owns a storage at a time; there is no cross-process locking'. The SQLite adapter only sets WAL and synchronous=NORMAL (^/packages/chord/src/sqlite/node.ts:237-239), with no exclusive locking or owner lease, and resume() starts every pending task (README.md:122-125).
gaps.impact: Two processes opening the same storage (overlapping restarts, a second replica) both resume pending work: replay-safe tools, generations and child tasks run twice, duplicating side effects and spend; concurrent JSONL appends can interleave.
gaps.fix: Acquire an exclusive owner lease at open (a lease row with expiry and heartbeat, or an OS advisory lock), fail with a typed error when it is held, and add a two-process test.

gaps.title: Breaking changes ship in patch and minor releases of a 1.x package
gaps.case: CHANGELOG.md lists Breaking Changes in 1.0.3 and 1.0.4 (both 2026-10-05, CHANGELOG.md:123-170), 1.1.0 (CHANGELOG.md:97-103), 1.2.0 (CHANGELOG.md:57-66) and Unreleased, whose SQLite schema v2 migration cannot be rolled back (CHANGELOG.md:9). Versions are lockstep across the monorepo (^/scripts/publish.mjs:34) and agents are told not to preserve backward compatibility (^/AGENTS.md:26); README.md:3 says the API changes without notice.
gaps.impact: Consumers using normal caret ranges (^1.3.0) receive breaking API and storage changes automatically; databases migrated by a newer release block rollback; 8 releases in 15 days outpace downstream users.
gaps.fix: Publish pi-durable as 0.x or under a 'next' dist-tag until stable, or bump the major version for breaking changes (decouple it from lockstep), and gate releases on an API report diff.

gaps.title: Untrusted content is not separated from instructions and injection is untested
gaps.case: ^/SECURITY.md:19-22 says injection through repository files 'cannot be protected against' and ^/SECURITY.md:56 puts prompt injection out of scope; rg finds no untrusted-content handling in packages/durable/src, docs/spec.md or README.md; file contents and tool results enter the context as ordinary entries.
gaps.impact: OWASP LLM01: instructions embedded in files, command output or subagent answers can steer tool calls, and hosts have no labelled channel or taint signal to build policy on.
gaps.fix: Record provenance (model, user, tool, file) on context entries and expose it to beforeTool hooks, and add an injection regression corpus run with the faux provider in CI.

gaps.title: Published tarball lacks the license text and releases have no SBOM
gaps.case: packages/durable contains no LICENSE file; package.json:108-112 ships dist, README.md and CHANGELOG.md; ^/scripts/package-artifacts.mjs:28 runs npm pack in the package directory; the MIT text is only at ^/LICENSE:1-3; no SBOM step exists in ^/.github/workflows/build-binaries.yml.
gaps.impact: MIT requires the copyright and permission notice in copies; compliance scanners find no license file in the tarball; SBOM expectations under the EU CRA (from Dec 2027) are unmet.
gaps.fix: Copy LICENSE into each package at pack time, generate a CycloneDX SBOM per release and attest it with the npm provenance, and publish the reviewed advisory ledger as VEX.

gaps.title: No property, fuzz or mutation testing for parsers and replay logic
gaps.case: The probes found no property, fuzz or mutation testing; untested by generated inputs are the hand-written EXIF/TIFF parser (src/images/exif.ts:4-60), JSONL torn-tail recovery (docs/spec.md:5446-5448) and code-mode replay divergence detection (README.md:366).
gaps.impact: Malformed images or torn JSONL files exercise paths covered only by a few hand-made cases; replay divergence bugs could resume a script on the wrong path.
gaps.fix: Add fast-check properties for JSONL recovery and code-mode replay, a fuzz target for image header and EXIF parsing, and track a mutation score for scheduler state transitions.

gaps.title: Benchmark numbers without environment, repetitions or stored results
gaps.case: CHANGELOG.md:87 (32,000 appends: 1.4 s instead of 11.3 s), CHANGELOG.md:93 (500 owned tasks: 12 s to 50 ms; 8000 nested calls: 2.7 s instead of 18.8 s) and README.md:810 (about 23 MB peak RSS) come from single-run scripts (test/document-append-bench.ts:1-7) with no results files (probe claims.harness: result files 0) and no CI run.
gaps.impact: The numbers cannot be checked on other machines or guarded against regression.
gaps.fix: Record hardware, Node version, repetitions, medians and intervals in a results file per release, and run a reduced benchmark set in CI with thresholds.

gaps.title: JSONL storage keeps the whole history in memory and does not fsync by default
gaps.case: README.md:763 says JSONL 'keeps the whole history in memory too, so memory grows with it'; fsync defaults to false (src/storage/jsonl/storage.ts:257), so acknowledged commits may be lost on power or host failure (docs/spec.md:5600-5602).
gaps.impact: Long-running agents on JSONL storage grow memory without bound and can lose acknowledged commits on host failure.
gaps.fix: Index and page JSONL reads instead of holding all records, and make the durability choice an explicit open option (or default fsync to on).

opps.title: SBOM and VEX from the existing advisory ledger
