targets.name: laya
targets.head: ffc142012af63d015fa19f05f29f9c5ff329a2cc
targets.scope_notes: Profile ml-system: three checkpoints plus their inference runtimes, ports and evaluation harness. uses_llm=true because laya ships an MCP server and agent-framework integrations executed by agents (it calls no LLM); executes_code=false because the shipped package is CI-gated against subprocess/eval and only dev scripts spawn processes; has_ui=false because the web playground is an example outside the published package; network_service (laya-serve), parses_untrusted (HTTP bodies, Hub model files), heavy_compute (GPU training and inference) and distributed (PyPI, npm, Maven) are true; uses_crypto=false because cryptography is limited to SHA-256 integrity digests and constant-time token comparison, with no signing, encryption or key exchange for SEC-9 to assess. Static review at ffc1420 (shallow clone); weights on Hugging Face were not reachable, so behaviour claims were checked against committed result files, not reruns.

gaps.title: Agent-facing descriptions claim calibrated probabilities the shipped checkpoints do not have
gaps.case: laya/mcp/server.py:95-101 tells every MCP client 'noul (calibrated P(true))' and 'No text generation, so no hallucination'; pyproject.toml:8 says 'with calibrated probabilities'. README.md:1578-1580 and research/results/t4_colab_benchmark.json (calibration_repair.mean_ece_shipped 0.4656 for laya, 0.3135 for laya-multilingual, which ships all-1.0 temperatures) show both checkpoints over-confident as shipped.
gaps.impact: Agents and integrators that read tool descriptions, not the README, act on raw probabilities as if calibrated (OWASP LLM09 misinformation); confident wrong answers are framed as impossible.
gaps.fix: Reword the descriptions and package metadata to 'probabilities; fit temperatures before thresholding', ship fitted temperatures for laya-multilingual, and add a test that fails when a description claims calibration that the checkpoint's evidence state (laya/evidence.py) does not show.

gaps.title: Checkpoints, datasets and the regression baseline are unpinned by default
gaps.case: laya/revisions.py:77-79 returns no revision unless the caller or LAYA_REVISION asks; docs/security.md:3-6 confirms the Hub default revision is used. The weekly gate runs research/eval/laya_eval.py --model convaiinnovations/laya with no revision (.github/workflows/evals.yml:54-58), datasets load without a revision (research/eval/laya_eval.py:104), and the baseline research/results/eval_english_51_languages.json records no model revision.
gaps.impact: A changed or compromised Hub repository changes every default deployment's decisions (including guardrail presets), and the regression gate silently compares against a moving target.
gaps.fix: Default the published checkpoints to PINNED_REVISIONS with an explicit opt-out, pin dataset revisions in the harnesses, and write model and dataset revisions into every report and baseline.

gaps.title: laya-serve listens on all interfaces without authentication by default
gaps.case: laya/serve.py:23 and laya/serve.py:1593 default LAYA_HOST to 0.0.0.0; laya/serve.py:39 leaves LAYA_API_KEY unset, which disables authentication; SECURITY.md:64-66 documents this as a warning rather than changing it.
gaps.impact: Unauthenticated network access to inference and server metadata on any host where laya-serve is started without extra configuration; conflicts with the CRA secure-by-default obligation from Dec 2027.
gaps.fix: Default to 127.0.0.1, and refuse to bind a non-loopback address without LAYA_API_KEY unless an explicit opt-out flag is set; test both in tests/test_serve.py.

gaps.title: Headline accuracy and throughput claims without committed results
gaps.case: README.md:89 presents 0.766 (fine-tuned) against 0.362 with no caveat; tests/test_doc_tables.py:362-367 lists 'README.md typed-decisions rows: no committed artifact for the fine-tuned checkpoint' and 'README.md / BENCHMARKS.md 103-332 q/s throughput: hand-picked from a range spanning 55-553'.
gaps.impact: The most prominent accuracy claim and the throughput claim cannot be reproduced from the repository.
gaps.fix: Commit the fine-tuning evaluation output (seed, n, checkpoint revision) and generate the README cells from it; replace the throughput range with the measured distribution from a committed file.

gaps.title: Calibration comparison with Jev is not on matched data
gaps.case: README.md:1505 claims ECE 0.081 vs 0.246, '3x better'. 0.081 is the mean over 49 suites after a per-suite refit (t4_colab_benchmark.json calibration_repair.laya.mean_ece_refit 0.0812); 0.246 comes from a different third-party study (research/README.md:176-177). On the one shared benchmark Jev's published ECE 0.144 is lower than laya-typed-decisions' 0.213 (README.md:1526-1531).
gaps.impact: Readers and tool-selecting agents take a cross-study number as a head-to-head result.
gaps.fix: Compare only on matched data, or mark the row as non-comparable and move it out of the headline table.

gaps.title: Supported-versions table is stale and no regulatory position exists
gaps.case: SECURITY.md:13-15 lists 0.3.x as the current line while pyproject.toml:7 ships 0.4.12; no compliance document exists (probe meta.compliance: 0 documents) although docs/use-cases.md:238-262 shows clinical/HIPAA routing.
gaps.impact: Users cannot tell whether 0.4.x receives security fixes; CRA vulnerability-reporting duties (from 11 Sep 2026) and support-period declarations are unaddressed.
gaps.fix: Generate the support table at release time (test it against pyproject), declare a support period, and add a short CRA/AI Act position for the library and the HTTP server.

gaps.title: Single maintainer for seven implementations
gaps.case: SECURITY.md:27-31 names one maintainer; no CODEOWNERS or governance document (probes meta.codeowners, meta.governance); the repository ships Python, TypeScript, Rust, Go, Java and .NET implementations and two SDKs.
gaps.impact: Security fixes and parity work stall if the maintainer is unavailable; port lanes are already advisory.
gaps.fix: Add CODEOWNERS per port, a governance and succession note, and a second maintainer with release rights.

gaps.title: Batch scoring and training cannot resume after a crash
gaps.case: laya/cli.py:361-404 builds every request, makes one predict_batch call (line 398) and prints only after it returns; laya/train.py:1125-1130 saves checkpoint_latest per epoch but 'rg -n -i resume laya/' finds no resume path.
gaps.impact: A kill during a large batch loses all results; a killed training run repeats the partial epoch and loses optimizer state.
gaps.fix: Stream results per chunk as JSONL with a skip-completed option, and add --resume from checkpoint_latest with optimizer state.

gaps.title: No SBOM and no lock for the Python package and image
gaps.case: probe ci.sbom: found=false; probe deps.lockfiles lists only TypeScript, Rust, Go and Nix locks; pyproject.toml:27-33 uses ranges and Dockerfile:30 runs pip install ".[serve]" unpinned.
gaps.impact: Container builds are not reproducible and SBOM obligations (CRA, Dec 2027) are unprepared.
gaps.fix: Lock the Python dependencies used by the image, generate a CycloneDX SBOM per release, and publish verify/checkpoints.json as the model part of an AI-BOM.

gaps.title: Agents get a prose-only HTTP contract and a repetitive MCP catalog
gaps.case: laya/serve.py:1331-1332 and 1428-1429 read raw Request bodies, so OpenAPI has no request schema; laya/mcp/server.py declares no tool annotations, and its descriptions total at least 12,613 bytes with _GUARDRAILS (378 B) repeated 9 times and _CONTROLS_DOC (1,151 B) 5 times (AST measurement).
gaps.impact: Agents pay several thousand tokens per catalog load, cannot validate HTTP calls against a schema, and hosts cannot auto-approve the read-only tools.
gaps.fix: Declare pydantic request and response models for both routes, add readOnlyHint annotations, and move shared guidance into one MCP resource or the laya_status tool.

opps.title: Publish the typed-decision record as a versioned JSON Schema
opps.description: The answer object (choice/score/noul, probabilities, answer_confidence, abstention state and threshold, usage with truncation and collapsed options, routing) is consistent across the Python host, its ports and laya-coreml, but exists only in code and prose. A published schema lets REA/rex evidence records, strix-style coverage ledgers and agent harnesses (orca, t3code, pandacode, pi) consume decisions without reading prose, and lets contract drift fail CI.

opps.title: Extract a torch-free calibration and abstention kernel
opps.description: Temperature fitting, binning, per-bucket abstention thresholds at a target error and the confidence gate are numpy logic, but laya/calibrate.py imports torch at module scope, so laya's own evidence module cannot import it and laya-coreml carries a modified copy with lazy imports. my-jev's bench.py and RE4exa rex's epistemics.calibrate (Wilson intervals, target-error advice) reimplement the same metrics. One small package would serve all four and add the per-class intervals laya lacks.

opps.title: Cut the MCP catalog and make its claims honest
opps.description: Move the repeated guardrail, model and controls text into one resource, add readOnly annotations and replace 'calibrated P(true)' and 'no hallucination' with measured wording. The same server is copied byte-for-byte into laya-coreml, so the fix reaches both.

opps.title: Offline, on-device typed decisions with declared cost per decision
opps.description: laya already runs offline (HF_HUB_OFFLINE, ModelScope mirror), in the browser through ONNX Runtime Web, and on Apple Silicon through laya-coreml, which measures joules per decision. Publishing latency and energy per checkpoint and runtime would let the Router pick the cheapest adequate path as on-device inference and energy pricing become requirements.

opps.title: Guard-plus-abstention screen for agent harnesses, measured on their own fixtures
opps.description: agent-sandbox-lockdown already has human approval for writes, a JSONL tool-call log and a planted document-shaped prompt injection. laya's guard preset with abstention could screen tool outputs before they reach the LLM and route low-confidence cases to the existing approval step. #781 shows the guard misses document-shaped injections, so the composition should start as a held-out benchmark on that fixture, not as a safety claim.

opps.title: One array-based backend contract for every host
opps.description: The backend contract hands torch tensors to a backend, so the ONNX path is a second host class and the Core ML and MLX ports copy the whole host (router, serve, MCP, evals, hooks) and re-sync it by hand. An array-in/array-out contract would let ONNX, Core ML, MLX and future runtimes plug in without duplicating host semantics.

reeng.component: laya-serve defaults (laya/serve.py main and create_app)
reeng.gain: No unauthenticated network exposure by default; OPS-3 from 2 to 3
reeng.measure: Tests asserting the default bind is 127.0.0.1 and that a non-loopback bind without LAYA_API_KEY refuses to start; SECURITY.md hardening section updated

reeng.component: Evaluation lane (research/eval/laya_eval.py, .github/workflows/evals.yml, research/results baselines)
reeng.gain: Headline accuracy and calibration claims reproducible from the repository for all three checkpoints
reeng.measure: Unbacked-claim list in tests/test_doc_tables.py goes from 4 to 0; every report records checkpoint and dataset revisions; the weekly gate covers 3 checkpoints instead of 1

reeng.component: Calibration and abstention kernel (laya/calibrate.py, laya/confidence.py, metric code in laya/evals.py)
reeng.gain: One torch-free implementation shared by laya, laya-coreml, my-jev and rex, with per-class intervals added
reeng.measure: Importing the kernel with torch blocked succeeds (tests/test_lazy_import.py pattern); laya-coreml's calibrate.py diff against upstream drops to 0 lines

reeng.component: HTTP and MCP contracts (laya/serve.py routes, laya/mcp/server.py)
reeng.gain: Machine-readable request and response schemas and a smaller, annotated tool catalog
reeng.measure: OpenAPI lists request schemas for both /v1/systemone routes; tools/list size from at least 12.6 KB to under 6 KB; readOnlyHint on all 10 tools

targets.name: t3code
targets.head: 7e289ae1f77b9137580688aaccf00d48906984ad
targets.scope_notes: agent-harness: T3 Code runs provider coding agents (Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Pi, ACP) that execute commands on the user's machine and serves them to web, desktop and mobile clients over a local server (127.0.0.1:3773), MCP and a cloud relay. All flags are set except heavy_compute, because model inference happens at the providers. This is a static review of commit 7e289ae1 (shallow clone), excluding the vendored .repos/ trees.

gaps.title: Agents run unsandboxed with approvals off by default
gaps.case: packages/contracts/src/providerPolicy.ts:32 sets DEFAULT_RUNTIME_MODE = 'full-access'. CodexAdapterV2.ts:709-716 maps it to approvalPolicy 'never' with sandbox dangerFullAccess, and ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:2006-2039 maps it to bypassPermissions. docs/user/permission-modes.md:8 confirms Full access is the initial default. T3 adds no OS boundary of its own; AgentScope only sets memory limits, and only on Linux.
gaps.impact: Excessive agency (OWASP LLM06): instructions injected through repository files, web pages or tool output can run commands and change files with no human checkpoint. Remote control from phones and the relay widens who can start such runs.
gaps.fix: Default new installs and new projects to Supervised or Auto (provider review). Require an explicit per-project opt-in to Full access, with a visible warning. Offer an OS-level boundary (container or egress allowlist) through the existing AgentScope.wrap hook.

gaps.title: Telemetry is on by default, opt-out is env-var only, and the UI calls linkable ids 'anonymous'
gaps.case: apps/server/src/telemetry/AnalyticsService.ts:81 defaults T3CODE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED to true. docs/user/telemetry.md:16-22 offers only an environment variable to opt out. WelcomeWizard.tsx:435 says 'anonymous usage data', while Identify.ts:181-189,255-268 reads ~/.codex/auth.json (id_token) and ~/.claude.json to derive owner ids, hashed with unsalted SHA-256 (telemetryId.ts:8-9). There is no DO_NOT_TRACK support and no settings toggle (rg).
gaps.impact: GDPR consent and transparency risk: pseudonymous, linkable account identifiers leave the machine by default, and the in-app wording understates this. Desktop users on Windows must set a user environment variable to opt out.
gaps.fix: Offer a first-run choice and a Settings toggle, honour DO_NOT_TRACK, and call the data pseudonymous. Replace unsalted hashes of provider account ids with a keyed hash or a random per-install id, and stop reading provider credential files for analytics identity.

gaps.title: Mutable action references in credentialed jobs; no dependency update or vulnerability scanning
gaps.case: Only 20 of 116 third-party action references are SHA-pinned (probe ci.pinned_actions). mobile-eas-preview.yml:100-102 runs expo/expo-github-action/continuous-deploy-fingerprint@main with EXPO_TOKEN. release.yml:705,860,876 uses softprops/action-gh-release@v3 in the contents:write release job, and ci.yml:426 uses dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable. There is no Dependabot or Renovate configuration and no audit or OSV step in any workflow.
gaps.impact: Supply-chain compromise: a moved upstream tag or branch executes in jobs that hold release, store or signing credentials, and known-vulnerable dependencies are never flagged.
gaps.fix: Pin every third-party action to a full commit SHA and let a bot update the pins. Add Renovate or Dependabot for npm, cargo and actions, a vulnerability gate (OSV-Scanner or pnpm audit), and OpenSSF Scorecard.

gaps.title: Release binaries have no provenance or signed checksums, and signing is silently optional
gaps.case: release.yml:752-765 writes SHA256SUMS unsigned. scripts/install.sh:194-206, scripts/install.ps1:171-186 and scripts/npm-launcher/t3.mjs:75-91 check archives only against SHA256SUMS from the same release. release-desktop.yml:446-486 logs 'signing disabled' and continues when secrets are missing, and docs/operations/release.md:58 calls signing optional. npm --provenance (release.yml:927) covers only the launcher, not the executables it downloads.
gaps.impact: All install and self-update paths (curl|sh, npx t3, t3 update, boot service, SSH environments) prove integrity but not authenticity. A tampered release asset or account would pass, and a misconfigured secret can ship an unsigned stable build.
gaps.fix: Attest the archives and installers (GitHub artifact attestations or Sigstore) and sign SHA256SUMS. Verify the signature in install.sh, install.ps1, the npm launcher and t3 update. Fail stable and nightly releases when signing secrets are absent.

gaps.title: MCP tool catalog is large and unmeasured
gaps.case: There are 83 Tool.make definitions under apps/server/src/mcp (non-test), with at least 38,362 characters of description text before JSON-schema structure (33,550 in toolkits/*/tools.ts, 4,812 in packages/contracts MCP schemas). All toolkits are registered on one endpoint for every provider session (docs/orchestration-v2/orchestrator-mcp-server.md:36-37), and no test measures tools/list size.
gaps.impact: Each provider session pays an estimated 9.6k+ tokens of catalog per turn (at 4 characters per token), large menus degrade tool selection, and catalog regressions go unseen.
gaps.fix: Measure tools/list bytes in CI with a budget, next to the existing transfer budgets. Register the preview, device and pull-request toolkits only when the session can use them, and shorten descriptions.

gaps.title: No per-task budgets for agent runs, delegations or schedules
gaps.case: Searching apps/server/src and packages/contracts/src for maxTurns, tokenBudget, costLimit or turnTimeout finds only the Codex goal tokenBudget passthrough (CodexAdapterV2.ts:940). delegate_task and scheduled tasks take no budget (docs/orchestration-v2/orchestrator-mcp-server.md:225-260), and usage is reported only after the fact (docs/user/usage.md:7-14).
gaps.impact: Unbounded consumption (OWASP LLM10): delegated, scheduled or webhook-triggered agents can loop until provider subscription limits stop them, and cost becomes visible only afterwards.
gaps.fix: Add token, wall-clock and call budgets to the runtime policy for runs, delegated tasks and schedules, enforce them in the orchestrator, and report spend against the budget per run.

gaps.title: Headline claims have no source, method or date
gaps.case: README.md:3 says 'best-in-class mobile app' and README.md:11 'performant'. AGENTS.md:9 says 'over 500,000 users'. apps/marketing/src/lib/site.ts:9-12 hard-codes users '500,000' and githubStars '24k+', which index.astro:119 renders.
gaps.impact: People and agents choosing tools from descriptions get claims they cannot check, and the hard-coded counts drift silently.
gaps.fix: Derive the user count from the analytics pipeline with method and date, or remove it. Link performance claims to the CI transfer-budget report, and drop unsupported superlatives.

gaps.title: No SBOM, support period or CRA position for a widely distributed product
gaps.case: Probe ci.sbom found no SBOM generation. .github/SECURITY.md:1-8 lists no supported versions, and probe evo.support found no support period. rg finds no mention of the Cyber Resilience Act, AI Act or Accessibility Act in docs or the marketing site. The product ships through the App Store, Google Play, npm, winget, scoop, brew and AUR.
gaps.impact: CRA vulnerability reporting applies from 11 Sep 2026, and SBOM and support-period duties from 11 Dec 2027. Enterprise buyers and downstream packagers lack component and support data.
gaps.fix: Emit CycloneDX or SPDX SBOMs per release from the existing license-manifest generator. State supported versions and a security-support period in SECURITY.md, and document the CRA role and obligations.

gaps.title: Accessibility and localisation are untested in a UI shipped to app stores
gaps.case: Probe ui.i18n found no i18n library or translation files. rg finds no axe, pa11y or lighthouse in the repo, although the web suite already runs Vitest browser tests in Chromium in CI (ci.yml:255-300).
gaps.impact: Screen-reader and keyboard regressions go undetected, non-English users are unsupported, and consumer-facing distribution carries EAA exposure.
gaps.fix: Add axe checks to the existing *.browser.test.tsx suites for key screens, move UI strings into a message catalogue, and state the accessibility conformance target.

gaps.title: No CODEOWNERS or governance for a codebase mostly written by agents
gaps.case: There is no .github/CODEOWNERS (probe meta.codeowners) and no governance file. AGENTS.md:41 says most contributions come from T3 Code itself. The only required check visible in the repo is the 'Check' job (ci.yml:494-496), and review requirements are not visible.
gaps.impact: Security-critical paths (apps/server/src/auth, apps/server/src/mcp, .github/workflows, release scripts) have no enforced owner review, and continuity rests on a small named group.
gaps.fix: Add CODEOWNERS for the auth, MCP, relay, release and workflow paths, require code-owner review there, and write a short governance and succession note.

gaps.title: MCP error contract drifts from its docs and has no retry semantics
gaps.case: packages/contracts/src/orchestratorMcp.ts:671-692 defines 16 failure codes. docs/orchestration-v2/orchestrator-mcp-server.md:509-524 lists 14, missing thread_credential_required and target_required. OrchestratorMcpFailure carries only code and message, while provider and VCS errors carry retryable (orchestrationV2.ts:1261, vcs.ts:122).
gaps.impact: Agents cannot tell from the contract which MCP failures to retry, and documented error handling misses real codes.
gaps.fix: Generate the code table from the schema, checked in CI, and add retryable plus an optional remediation field to OrchestratorMcpFailure.

gaps.title: Design index presents the shipped durable outbox as future work
gaps.case: docs/orchestration-v2/README.md:110-166 ('Tracked Follow-Up: Durable Effect Outbox') says the current pipeline uses reactors. apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/EffectOutbox.ts ships the outbox, and AGENTS.md:154 describes it as current.
gaps.impact: Maintainers and coding agents reading the design index get the wrong side-effect and recovery architecture.
gaps.fix: Rewrite or remove the section, as the project's own rule in AGENTS.md 'Documentation' requires ('rewrite or remove the affected text').

opps.title: One untrusted-content envelope for every injection channel
opps.description: T3 frames untrusted text in four ways: nonce-tagged blocks for webhooks, a JSON-encoded frame for captured windows, and prose preambles for transcripts and thread references. Standardising on the nonce-tagged envelope, with redaction and provenance fields, and publishing it with its tests would give one tested format and a shared injection corpus to pi, Orca and PandaCode, which also feed external content to agents.

opps.title: Capability-scoped MCP toolkits with a catalog budget
opps.description: Advertise only the toolkits a session can use: preview and device tools when a browser or device is attached, pull-request tools when a source-control account is linked. Add a tools/list byte budget to CI next to the transfer budgets. Baseline: 83 tools and at least 38,362 characters of descriptions.

opps.title: Turn the license-manifest generator into per-release SBOMs
opps.description: The build already walks the production dependency closure for web, server, desktop and mobile, and fails when license data is missing. Emitting CycloneDX or SPDX from the same walk, attested with the release, covers the CRA SBOM duty (Dec 2027) and SEC-4 at low cost.

opps.title: Run Full-access agents inside agent-sandbox-lockdown-style boundaries via AgentScope.wrap
opps.description: Every provider launch already goes through AgentScope.wrap, which today adds systemd memory scopes on Linux. agent-sandbox-lockdown ships the missing boundary: DNS and egress-proxy allowlists, least-privilege tools, a step cap, a JSONL tool log and a kill switch. Composing the two gives Full-access sessions an OS-level boundary without changing provider adapters, and closes the main AGT-2 gap.

opps.title: Fetch vendored reference trees on demand instead of committing them
opps.description: 21,835 of 28,433 tracked files (77%, 218 MB on disk) are git subtrees under .repos/ that agents read as references. Every CI job sparse-excludes them, and scripts/sync-reference-repos.ts already syncs them at pinned refs. Fetching them on demand at those pins keeps the agent benefit while shrinking clones and code-search noise.

opps.title: Shared adapter conformance kit for coding-agent GUIs
opps.description: T3, Orca and PandaCode all wrap the same CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi). T3 has the strongest verification asset: a provider-neutral replay runtime (packages/provider-testing), the ProviderAdapterV2 contract with capability records (packages/provider-core), recorders for six providers, and 91 recorded scenarios (149 NDJSON transcripts, 8.0 MB). Publishing them as a versioned conformance suite would let each GUI test adapters against the same recorded behaviour and catch provider protocol drift once for all of them. Today both packages are private and coupled to Effect v4.

opps.title: Extract the SQLite durable command and effect kernel
opps.description: EventSink, CommandReceiptStore and EffectOutbox form a compact, local-first durable-execution core: one-transaction commit, leased claims, replay-safe versus process-bound effect classes, process-loss reconciliation and a restart-chain cap. absurd covers the same ground on Postgres, and pi-durable at the agent-conversation level. A shared contract for these semantics, with T3's kernel as the SQLite implementation, would let harnesses reuse proven crash semantics instead of reimplementing them. The effect-type registry must be split from orchestration types first.

reeng.component: Release and CI supply chain (.github/workflows/*, scripts/install.sh, scripts/install.ps1, scripts/npm-launcher/t3.mjs, packages/shared/src/cliRelease.ts)
reeng.gain: Authenticity, not just integrity, on every install and self-update path, and no mutable third-party code in credentialed jobs.
reeng.measure: SHA-pinned third-party action refs go from 20/116 to 116/116 (rqs probe ci.pinned_actions). All release assets carry attestations (from 0). An installer test rejects a tampered SHA256SUMS. A stable release fails when signing secrets are absent.

reeng.component: Safe defaults: packages/contracts/src/providerPolicy.ts:32 (runtime mode), apps/server/src/telemetry/AnalyticsService.ts:81 and Identify.ts (telemetry consent and identity)
reeng.gain: Least agency and consent by default, without removing any capability.
reeng.measure: A contract test asserts the default runtime mode is not full-access. Track the share of new threads started in Full access (existing feature.used analytics). AnalyticsService tests cover the toggle and DO_NOT_TRACK. PRV-1 and AGT-2 re-scored at 3 or higher.

reeng.component: Largest modules: Orchestrator.ts (12,143 lines), ClaudeAdapterV2.ts (10,417), ChatView.tsx (8,994), provider-acp adapter.ts (8,514), CodexAdapterV2.ts (7,528)
reeng.gain: Smaller units for review and for agent context, and fewer merge conflicts in a very high-PR-volume repo.
reeng.measure: Non-test source files over 3,000 lines drop from 26 to 10 or fewer, with maximum file size tracked per release by a CI size budget.

reeng.component: MCP server (apps/server/src/mcp, 83 tools in 11 toolkits)
reeng.gain: Lower per-turn context cost and better tool selection for every provider session.
reeng.measure: tools/list bytes per session type are measured in CI. Baseline: at least 38,362 description characters across 83 tools. Target: 50% or less for sessions with no preview or device attached.

targets.name: laya-coreml
targets.head: 7b363344ffe8da77cc50da056181be1a3c5c405c
targets.scope_notes: Profile ml-system: a Core ML conversion and inference runtime for laya checkpoints plus six published bundles. uses_llm=true (MCP server and agent-framework integrations executed by agents; no LLM is called); has_ui=true because the wheel ships the Rich terminal Snake demo (laya-coreml-snake); executes_code=false (only fixed helper commands such as sysctl and ffmpeg); network_service (laya-coreml-serve), parses_untrusted (HTTP bodies, downloaded .mlpackage graphs compiled by native Core ML), heavy_compute (conversion and on-device inference with measured energy) and distributed (PyPI, Hugging Face) are true; uses_crypto=false (SHA-256 integrity checks and a content-addressed cache only, no signing, encryption or key exchange). Static review at 7b36334 (shallow clone); Hugging Face bundles and cards were not reachable and no Apple hardware was available, so speed, energy and fidelity claims were checked against committed result files.

gaps.title: PyPI releases use a long-lived token with attestations disabled
gaps.case: .github/workflows/release.yml:57-72: the publish job holds contents: write and authenticates with password: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }} with attestations: false, in the same job and without a protected environment.
gaps.impact: Users cannot verify that a wheel was built from this repository, and a leaked token allows publishing arbitrary releases.
gaps.fix: Switch to PyPI trusted publishing (id-token: write) with attestations on, split the GitHub-release step into its own job, and add a protected environment.

gaps.title: No security policy or vulnerability contact
gaps.case: No SECURITY.md (probe meta.security_policy found=false) and no security, vulnerability or threat text in any Markdown file, although the wheel ships an HTTP server and loads downloaded model packages.
gaps.impact: Reporters have no private channel; CRA vulnerability-reporting duties apply from 11 Sep 2026.
gaps.fix: Add SECURITY.md with a private reporting channel, response targets and trust boundaries (Hub bundles, HTTP server, MCP server).

gaps.title: HTTP server is open on all interfaces by default and its controls are undocumented
gaps.case: laya_coreml/serve.py:23 and laya_coreml/serve.py:1697 default LAYA_HOST to 0.0.0.0; laya_coreml/serve.py:39 leaves authentication off unless LAYA_API_KEY is set; the Markdown docs mention 6 LAYA_* variables while the package reads about 25.
gaps.impact: Starting laya-coreml-serve on a shared network exposes unauthenticated inference.
gaps.fix: Default to 127.0.0.1, refuse non-loopback binds without LAYA_API_KEY, and document every variable in docs/USAGE.md.

gaps.title: Bundle checksums are recorded but not verified, and default revisions are unpinned
gaps.case: scripts/prepare_hub.py:155-160 writes per-file SHA-256 into coreml_config.json, but laya_coreml/agent.py:82 verifies digests only when expected_sha256 or LAYA_SHA256_DIGESTS is given, and laya_coreml/hub.py:41-49 applies BUNDLE_REVISIONS only when a revision is requested.
gaps.impact: A swapped or corrupted Hub bundle reaches the native Core ML compiler unverified.
gaps.fix: Verify the manifest's recorded checksums on every load and pin BUNDLE_REVISIONS for built-in bundles by default, with an explicit opt-out.

gaps.title: Agent-facing MCP descriptions state upstream latency and a calibration claim the port contradicts
gaps.case: laya_coreml/mcp/server.py:95-101 tells MCP clients 'One forward pass ~33ms (GPU) / ~200ms (CPU)' and 'noul (calibrated P(true))'; BENCHMARKS.md:15-22 measures 11.28-13.71 ms on CPU+GPU and 82.54 ms on CPU for this runtime, and README.md:220-222 says shipped confidences need held-out calibration.
gaps.impact: Agents budget time and set thresholds on numbers that do not describe this runtime.
gaps.fix: Generate the description's latency line from the port's measured results and reword the calibration claim.

gaps.title: Real-bundle fidelity and performance are validated only on the maintainer's machine
gaps.case: docs/UPSTREAM_0412_PROGRESS.json points to local /tmp logs; benchmarks/results/release-validation.json and v051-*-validation.json are produced locally; .github/workflows/ci.yml runs only tiny-model and host tests.
gaps.impact: A fidelity regression between qualification runs goes unnoticed, and no third party has reproduced the speed or energy figures.
gaps.fix: Add a macOS CI job that downloads one small pinned bundle (for example the ANE L96 package) and runs benchmarks/release_validate.py with the 0.02 drift gate.

gaps.title: No dependency updates, vulnerability scanning or secret scanning
gaps.case: Probes deps.update_bot and ci.security_scans find nothing; .github/workflows/ci.yml:31 installs from pyproject ranges rather than the committed uv.lock.
gaps.impact: Known vulnerabilities in coremltools, FastAPI, uvicorn or mcp go unnoticed, and CI does not test the locked set users of the lock would get.
gaps.fix: Add Dependabot, pip-audit and gitleaks jobs, and install from uv.lock in CI.

gaps.title: Declared platform matrix is not tested
gaps.case: README.md:35 declares macOS 15+ and Python 3.11-3.13; .github/workflows/ci.yml:14 and :29 test macos-26 and Python 3.12 only.
gaps.impact: Breakage on macOS 15 or Python 3.11/3.13 ships undetected.
gaps.fix: Add macos-15 and Python 3.11/3.13 to the matrix, or narrow the declared support.

gaps.title: Single maintainer hand-syncs a mirrored upstream host
gaps.case: NOTICE records three manual synchronisation rounds with upstream (4aa6761, 1adc59f, v0.4.12); one git author; no CODEOWNERS or governance.
gaps.impact: Upstream security and behaviour fixes reach the port only when the maintainer re-syncs.
gaps.fix: Add a scheduled CI job that compares the pinned upstream commit with the latest upstream tag and opens an issue, plus a governance and succession note.

opps.title: Extract the Apple Silicon energy-measurement harness
opps.description: The unprivileged PSTR sampler, alternating-block campaign, idle subtraction, anomaly rejection and cycle bootstrap are independent of laya and would serve any on-device inference project (laya-mlx, MLX or Core ML models) that needs joules per functional unit.

opps.title: Carry upstream weight digests into every decision for cross-repo evidence
opps.description: The port records the upstream weights' SHA-256 (891102d3... for the English checkpoint), the same digest laya's verify/checkpoints.json lists. Emitting source_weights_sha256 and package_sha256 in each result's routing block would let REA/rex evidence records cite exactly which weights and graph produced a decision, across both runtimes.

opps.title: Declared cost per decision for automatic low-energy routing
opps.description: Latency and joules per decision are measured per bundle but live only in result files. Publishing them in each bundle manifest would let Router choose the cheapest bundle that fits an input, as on-device inference and energy pricing become procurement requirements.

opps.title: Port-qualification kit for every laya runtime
opps.description: AST-identity and output-equality tests against pinned upstream, golden comparisons from the official FP32 model with a drift gate, repeated-call stability and running upstream's own suites under a rewritten namespace together form a qualification kit. Upstream maintains six ports with their own golden tooling; one shared kit would qualify ONNX, TypeScript, Rust, Go, Java, .NET, MLX and Ascend ports the same way.

opps.title: Fold the mirrored host into upstream behind an array backend
opps.description: About 20k lines of router, server, MCP, evaluation, hooks and integrations mirror upstream and are re-synced by hand; the AST-identity tests show they are meant to be identical. If upstream's backend contract accepted arrays instead of torch tensors, the port could ship only its Core ML runtime and artefact handling.

reeng.component: Release pipeline (.github/workflows/release.yml) and Hub bundle publication
reeng.gain: Verifiable provenance for wheels and no long-lived publishing secret
reeng.measure: PEP 740 attestations present on the next PyPI release; no PYPI_API_TOKEN referenced in workflows; bundles uploaded from CI or with signed manifests

reeng.component: Security baseline (SECURITY.md, laya_coreml/serve.py defaults, CI scanners)
reeng.gain: A reporting channel, safe server defaults and dependency and secret scanning
reeng.measure: Probes meta.security_policy, deps.update_bot and ci.security_scans report found=true; a test asserts the default bind is 127.0.0.1

reeng.component: Bundle loading (laya_coreml/hub.py, laya_coreml/agent.py)
reeng.gain: Tampered or swapped bundles are rejected before native compilation
reeng.measure: A test with one modified file in a bundle fails to load; load-time overhead in ms recorded for the 1024-token bundle

reeng.component: Host layer shared with upstream laya (router, serve, mcp, evals, hooks, integrations)
reeng.gain: No manual re-sync per upstream release and a much smaller port
reeng.measure: Changed lines against upstream for router/serve/mcp/evals fall from 676/298/241/428 towards zero; manual sync rounds per upstream release fall to 0

targets.name: orca
targets.head: 997d34b04389665795966ec4c0325b5cbfabf9ee
targets.scope_notes: Profile agent-harness: an Electron desktop IDE plus CLI, headless orcad server, mobile companion and cloud relay that launches and orchestrates third-party coding-agent CLIs on the user's machine; flags all set except heavy_compute, because it runs agents, executes commands, listens on loopback/LAN sockets, parses agent terminal output, repo files and web pages, uses NaCl/Ed25519/AES-GCM, and ships signed installers, while model inference runs in the user's own agents and providers. Static review of commit 997d34b0 (shallow clone); nothing was built or run.

gaps.title: Every launched agent defaults to maximum agency
gaps.case: src/shared/tui-agent-launch-defaults.ts:18-19 sets DEFAULT_TUI_AGENT_ARGS = YOLO_TUI_AGENT_ARGS; src/shared/tui-agent-permissions.ts:17 maps Codex to --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox (Claude, Gemini, Copilot and others likewise at lines 13-43); src/main/agent-trust-presets.ts:10-27 pre-writes Cursor, Copilot and Codex folder-trust markers so their 'trust this folder?' prompt never appears.
gaps.impact: Agents run shell commands without approval as the user, outside the worktree, including actions induced by untrusted repository or web content (excessive agency, OWASP LLM06). This conflicts with the secure-by-default configuration duty of the EU CRA (from 2027-12-11).
gaps.fix: Default new installs to Manual or each agent's own sandboxed mode, make the bypass flag an explicit per-repository opt-in, and write third-party trust markers only after the user confirms the folder.

gaps.title: Repo setup-script trust is enforced only in the desktop renderer
gaps.case: src/shared/constants.ts:145 defaults setupRunPolicy to 'run-by-default'; the main-process gate src/main/effective-hook-config.ts:64-78 decides from that policy alone; trust records are written by the renderer (src/renderer/src/store/slices/ui/ui-slice-trust-actions.ts:7-20) and `rg trustedOrcaHooks src` outside src/renderer finds only types and defaults; the CLI `--setup` flag defaults to inherit (src/cli/flag-help-text.ts:65) and the runtime create path consults only the policy (src/main/runtime/runtime-local-worktree-create.ts:87-99).
gaps.impact: Setup commands committed in an untrusted clone's orca.yaml can run on worktree creation from the CLI, automations or the mobile app without the confirmation the desktop window shows (code execution from repository content; inferred from the main-process gate, full call graph not traced).
gaps.fix: Move the content-hash trust check into shouldRunSetupForCreate in the main process, require a trusted hash or an explicit interactive 'run', and default repositories with committed scripts to 'ask'.

gaps.title: Docs contradict the code on the sandbox boundary and on data flows
gaps.case: docs/site/content/docs/model/agents-sessions.mdx:63 says 'the worktree itself is the sandbox' while docs/site/content/docs/agents/supported.mdx:11-12 says a worktree is not a security sandbox; docs/site/content/docs/agents/usage-tracking.mdx:15 says 'No API calls, no extra auth' while src/main/rate-limits/claude-oauth-usage-request.ts:18,82 calls api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with the user's OAuth credentials; docs/site/content/docs/review/attribution.mdx:9 describes AI-line gutter markers, and searching src for attribution, provenance and gutter markers found no implementation.
gaps.impact: Users choosing a trust posture or reviewing data flows get wrong information about the security boundary and about credential use (misinformation; undisclosed processing).
gaps.fix: Correct both pages, remove or implement the attribution feature, and add a docs check that links feature and data-flow pages to code or tests.

gaps.title: Mutable action tags, a third-party agent action holding provider keys, and no dependency or repo-wide secret scanning
gaps.case: 15 of 570 third-party action references are SHA-pinned (probe ci.pinned_actions; actions/checkout@v6 x119); .github/workflows/pullfrog.yml:59-60,81,86-95 runs pullfrog/pullfrog@v0 with id-token: write and ten provider API keys; `rg 'pnpm audit|npm audit|osv-scanner|codeql|dependency-review' .github` returns nothing; Dependabot covers only ripgrep (.github/dependabot.yml:3-10); gitleaks and TruffleHog scan only cloud/ paths (.github/workflows/cloud-verify.yml:60-77).
gaps.impact: A moved tag or compromised action runs with repository tokens or can exfiltrate provider keys, and known-vulnerable dependencies or secrets committed to the desktop source go undetected (supply-chain compromise).
gaps.fix: Pin every action by full SHA with automated update PRs, give the review agent scoped short-lived credentials, and add osv-scanner or pnpm audit plus a repository-wide gitleaks job to PR CI.

gaps.title: No vulnerability disclosure policy, support period or regulatory position
gaps.case: No SECURITY.md or security contact (`git ls-files | grep -iE 'security(\.md|\.txt)'` returns nothing; probe meta.security_policy found=false); no support or end-of-life statement (probe evo.support found=false); no mention of the CRA, AI Act or accessibility law in README, docs or .github (probe meta.compliance mentions 0).
gaps.impact: Researchers have no reporting channel for a code-executing app with network listeners, E2EE pairing and a cloud relay, and the CRA vulnerability-reporting duties in force since 2026-09-11 and the support-period declaration due from 2027-12-11 are unprepared (coordinated-disclosure and regulatory risk).
gaps.fix: Publish SECURITY.md with contact, scope and response times; add a threat model covering agents, repository content, paired devices, the relay and plugins; state a support period; write a CRA and AI Act position note.

gaps.title: Releases ship without SBOM or provenance, and rule bundles are unsigned
gaps.case: No SBOM or VEX step (probe ci.sbom found=false); no attestation step (`rg 'attest-build-provenance|cosign|sigstore|slsa' .github/workflows` returns nothing); agent-state rule bundles are downloaded from a fixed GitHub release URL and accepted after schema validation only (src/main/runtime/agent-state-rules/agent-state-rules-live-update.ts:42-45,77-86).
gaps.impact: Users cannot verify which source and pipeline built a release or audit shipped components, and a tampered rule bundle would be accepted if TLS or the release account were compromised (integrity of agent-status detection).
gaps.fix: Generate a CycloneDX SBOM and SLSA provenance in release-cut.yml, publish checksums with verification steps, and sign rule bundles or pin their digests in the shipped app.

gaps.title: Telemetry is on for new installs without an in-product notice, and the docs list a fraction of the events
gaps.case: src/main/persistence/loading-store/loaded-cohort-migrations.ts:97-102 sets optedIn true for new installs; src/renderer/src/components/TelemetryFirstLaunchSurface.tsx:1-4 shows new users no first-launch surface; src/shared/telemetry-event-registry.ts defines 88 event types while docs/site/content/docs/telemetry.mdx:20-29 lists 9 categories and does not say collection is on by default.
gaps.impact: Users are enrolled without seeing a notice in the product, and the disclosure is not field by field (consent quality under GDPR and ePrivacy).
gaps.fix: Show a first-run notice to new installs (or make collection opt-in), and generate the docs event and field list from the registry in CI.

gaps.title: End-to-end suite is advisory and red on main
gaps.case: .github/workflows/pr.yml:1696-1703 leaves e2e out of the verify job's needs because 'the suite is currently red on main (every scheduled run)'; crash and resume journeys such as tests/e2e/agent-session-live-force-exit-resume.spec.ts live in that suite; Windows crash survival runs only on manual dispatch (.github/workflows/win-crash-survival-e2e.yml:12-13).
gaps.impact: Regressions in user journeys, including crash and resume paths, can merge unnoticed; 563 specs give less protection than their count suggests.
gaps.fix: Quarantine failing specs with owners and issue links, add the path-filtered e2e job to verify's needs, and schedule the crash-survival workflow.

gaps.title: Agent contract lacks effect annotations, argument schemas and distinct exit codes
gaps.case: src/cli/agent-context.ts:9-22 exports command names, usage strings and flag names only; CommandSpec.destructive (src/cli/command-spec.ts:6-7) is not exported; every CLI failure sets exit code 1 (src/cli/index.ts:74,100,205,223,248); no MCP server (probe agent.mcp found=false).
gaps.impact: Agents cannot tell destructive from read-only commands or validate arguments before calling one of 284 commands, and scripts cannot branch on the failure class without parsing JSON.
gaps.fix: Add readOnly, destructive and idempotent fields and a JSON Schema per command to agent-context schema v2, map error codes to documented exit codes, and serve the same contract over MCP.

gaps.title: Surface size and release churn outpace reviewability and ownership
gaps.case: 16,956 production TS/TSX files and 2,101,263 lines under src (git ls-files, tests and fixtures excluded); flat directories src/shared (2,903 entries), src/renderer/src/lib (1,286) and src/main/runtime (1,246); 97 workflows with 24,938 YAML lines; 982 entries in config/scripts; config/reliability-gates.jsonc is 1.88 MB with all 149 gates 'experimental'; version 1.4.214 and README.md:167 'we ship daily'; .github/CODEOWNERS:1-10 covers only localization and cloud.
gaps.impact: Review depth per change and the ability of a new maintainer or agent to navigate the code fall, and continuity depends on a small, partly unnamed owner set (maintainability and continuity risk).
gaps.fix: Group flat directories into domain modules with import rules, extend CODEOWNERS to core areas, keep release notes in the repository, and promote or retire experimental gates on their stated criteria.

gaps.title: Contributor docs and code comments reference files that are not in the repository
gaps.case: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md:168 points to release-rc.yml, which is absent from .github/workflows; src/shared/telemetry-property-schemas.ts:62 and src/preload/api/telemetry-api.ts:53 cite telemetry-plan.md and telemetry-error-tracking.md, of which 0 files are tracked.
gaps.impact: Contributors and agents follow references that do not exist, and the telemetry design rationale cited by the code cannot be reviewed.
gaps.fix: Fix or remove the references and extend the README link check to CONTRIBUTING and to code comments that cite documents.

opps.title: Produce CRA evidence from the existing release pipeline
opps.description: release-cut.yml already builds, signs (SignPath with signature checks, macOS notarization) and publishes every platform in CI. Adding a CycloneDX SBOM, SLSA provenance, a checksum manifest, VEX statements and a SECURITY and support-period statement turns existing steps into the evidence the CRA expects from 2027-12-11; the bundled ripgrep notices show the pattern for shipping license data.

opps.title: Publish @orca/process-host as a standalone package
opps.description: A 38-file package with no runtime npm dependencies, no Electron imports and a Node 18 floor that owns spawning, bounded output, cancellation, Windows .cmd shim and argument encoding, and process-tree termination with exit proof (src/packages/process-host/README.md:3; package.json engines '>=18', private, version 0.0.0). Other reviewed harnesses and installers (t3code, pandacode, caveman) spawn agent CLIs and face the same Windows quoting and orphan-process problems.

opps.title: Ship a locked-down container recipe as the default home for bypass-mode agents
opps.description: Orca already boots per-workspace environments, including local Docker containers, from orca.yaml recipes (docs/site/content/docs/ways-to-run.mdx:72-90) but launches agents in bypass mode on the host by default. agent-sandbox-lockdown provides the missing isolation layout: an internal-only network, CoreDNS and tinyproxy allowlists, a read-only workspace mount, one writable outbox, a kill file and a JSONL tool-call log. Packaging that layout as a built-in recipe turns 'no approvals, inside a locked container' into the default instead of 'no approvals on the host'.

opps.title: Program Status Protocol consumer SDK for other harnesses
opps.description: Orca parses the published Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501; spec link at src/shared/program-status/protocol.ts:2) with bounded fields and capability negotiation, and fuses it with hook events and declarative screen rules (src/main/runtime/agent-state-rules/). Pi emits the protocol (earendil-works/pi packages/tui/test/program-status.test.ts), while t3code and pandacode contain no reference to it (rg '7501|program-status' finds only incidental matches). Extracting the scanner, projector and rule engine as an SDK gives every harness the same agent-state signal without screen scraping.

opps.title: Serve the CLI and RPC contract over MCP with effect hints
opps.description: Agents already drive Orca through 284 CLI commands with a zod-validated envelope and idempotency keys, and the runtime holds zod parameter schemas for 748 RPC methods plus per-method permission classes (src/main/runtime/rpc/rpc-method-permission.ts). Generating a lazily loaded MCP catalog per namespace, with readOnly, destructive and idempotent hints derived from CommandSpec.destructive and the permission classes, lets any MCP host call Orca without prose or shell parsing.

opps.title: One shared agent-CLI registry across harnesses and installers
opps.description: Orca maintains per-agent permission flags (src/shared/tui-agent-permissions.ts:13-43), folder-trust marker formats (src/main/agent-trust-presets.ts), skill install paths (src/shared/skill-install-providers.ts) and resume commands (src/shared/agent-session-resume.ts). t3code (apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/Adapters), pandacode (src-tauri/src/slash_commands/{claude,codex,kimi}.rs) and caveman (agents/agents.json, agents/probe-installed.mjs) keep their own tables for the same CLIs. A versioned data package with contract tests against pinned CLI versions replaces four drifting copies.

opps.title: Reliability-gate manifest and ratchets as a reusable evidence ledger
opps.description: config/reliability-gates.jsonc records 149 gates with invariant, oracle, commands, dated evidence runs, runtime budgets, flake history, known gaps and promotion and demotion rules, validated in PR CI by config/scripts/check-reliability-gates.mjs, and 14 shrink-only ratchet baselines enforce debt reduction. Packaged as a schema plus checker, it gives other reviewed repositories (rea, strix, absurd) a machine-checkable ledger that maps onto RQS COR, REL and MNT-5 evidence.

targets.name: strix
targets.head: aa2036f22942eed3ecd142169289a256a2e7acb7

gaps.title: No security policy, threat model or disclosure channel
gaps.case: No SECURITY.md anywhere in the repo (meta.security_policy found=false); README.md:385 carries only an authorized-use warning.

gaps.title: Unverified install and unattested releases
gaps.case: README.md:84 and scripts/install.sh:154 fetch the release binary over curl|bash with no checksum/signature check; build-release.yml:100 uploads artifacts with no provenance/signing (ci.provenance found=false).

gaps.title: Documentation describes observability the code does not ship
gaps.case: docs/advanced/configuration.mdx:148-166 documents TRACELOOP/OTEL remote tracing and a local events.jsonl, but no OTEL/Traceloop/events.jsonl implementation exists in strix/ (grep).
gaps.impact: epistemic: operators relying on the documented audit/trace trail get nothing, and the doc overstates shipped capability.

gaps.title: Headline capability number is external and stale
gaps.case: benchmarks/README.md:24 cites a 96% XBEN result for Strix v0.4.0 while pyproject.toml:3 is 1.7.0; the harness and raw results live in an external repo (benchmarks/README.md:8), none committed here.
gaps.impact: epistemic: the flagship capability claim cannot be reproduced at the reviewed commit and is tied to an old version.
gaps.fix: Commit the harness and raw results (or a slim answer-key lane) and re-run it against the shipped version, dated.

gaps.title: No SBOM, VEX or third-party notices for a distributed bundle
gaps.case: No SBOM step in CI (ci.sbom found=false) and no NOTICE/third-party license file (meta.notices found=false), though the wheel bundles a Go sidecar and a prebuilt React viewer.
gaps.impact: compliance: EU CRA SBOM obligation (Dec 2027) unmet and third-party attribution debt.
gaps.fix: Generate a CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM per release and add a complete NOTICE file.

gaps.title: Untrusted-input parsers are not fuzzed
gaps.case: strix/utils/api_spec.py parses attacker-influenceable OpenAPI/Swagger/Postman specs; it has malformed-input unit tests (tests/test_api_spec.py:121) and a depth cap but no fuzzing, and there is no mutation/property testing anywhere (COR-3).
gaps.impact: correctness/robustness: parser edge cases on hostile input are unverified.
gaps.fix: Add fuzz targets for the spec parser and the other untrusted-input readers with size/recursion assertions.

gaps.title: Untrusted target content is not separated from instructions
gaps.case: The agent is designed to act on target-controlled content, but strix/agents/prompts/system_prompt.jinja does not mark an untrusted_content channel distinct from instructions, and there is no injection-resistance regression suite (agent.prompt_injection refs are sandbox/isolation, not channel separation).
gaps.impact: AI safety: an autonomous agent can be steered by instructions embedded in target content; mitigation currently rests on prompt wording, not a policy boundary.
gaps.fix: Label untrusted channels explicitly and add a held-out injection regression corpus run per model version (defensive, no technique detail needed).

gaps.title: Cryptography has no inventory, abstraction or PQC plan
gaps.case: AES-256 report encryption (strix/interface/viewer/report_pdf.py:679), PKCE S256 (strix/config/codex.py:169) and HMAC (sidecar) are used directly with no algorithm inventory, replaceable layer or post-quantum plan.
gaps.impact: horizon/compliance: CNSA 2.0 and the NIST 2030-35 transition are unprepared.
gaps.fix: Document a crypto inventory, route crypto through one abstraction, and publish a dated ML-KEM/ML-DSA migration plan.

gaps.title: No support period, changelog or SemVer policy
gaps.case: No committed CHANGELOG, no stated SemVer/migration policy (evo.semver) and no support/EOL window (evo.support found=false) for a PyPI-distributed product.
gaps.impact: evolution/compliance: downstreams cannot pin on compatibility or on a security-fix window (EU CRA support-period).
gaps.fix: Add a CHANGELOG with migration notes, state a SemVer policy and declare a support period.

opps.title: Extract the coverage-accounting record as a shared standard
opps.description: coverage.json separates declared scope, tested-clean, unexamined gaps and completeness caveats, and keeps agent-reported apart from machine-observed facts that contradict it. It is a self-contained, high-value artifact (dissection score 18) that rea (residual unknowns) and caveman could consume as a common coverage-record format.

opps.description: strix already spills oversized tool output to disk and retrieves it by path; caveman's byte-safe S0-S4 compressors and content-addressed CCR recovery handles would cut agent context cost further while keeping byte-exact recovery, sharing a retrieval-handle shape.

opps.title: Turn the report pipeline into a CRA/AI-Act evidence pipeline
opps.description: strix already emits SARIF 2.1.0 and coverage completeness and sells compliance-ready reports; adding SBOM/VEX and an AI-BOM to the release and report pipeline makes it a dated-obligation-ready output customers will need by 2027.

targets.name: absurd
targets.head: 3cfc64f10b0bef7ff159ec4e01a4ae76424c8d05
targets.scope_notes: Profile workflow-engine: a Postgres-only durable execution engine (sql/absurd.sql) with thin TS/Python/Go SDKs, the absurdctl CLI and the habitat dashboard (README.md:8-11, AGENTS.md:3-6). Flags checked against code: has_ui=true (habitat SolidJS UI, habitat/ui/src); network_service=true (habitat listens on :7890 and serves a JSON API, habitat/internal/config/config.go:15, habitat/internal/server/server.go:73-129); parses_untrusted=true because habitat decodes HTTP requests from any peer that reaches the port without authentication and absurdctl ingests remote SQL and a JSON index from GitHub (absurdctl:517-519, 645-679), not because of the probe's fetch count; executes_code=true (workers run user task code, absurdctl spawns psql, absurdctl:335); uses_llm=false (no model calls; the bundled 7.3 KB SKILL.md is assessed under INT-2/PERF-2 rather than AGT); uses_crypto=false (md5/random UUIDs only for naming, TLS delegated to drivers); distributed=true (npm, PyPI, GitHub Releases, Go module).

gaps.title: Habitat listens on all interfaces without authentication and exposes a write endpoint, while the docs describe a read-only localhost view
gaps.case: habitat/internal/config/config.go:15 defaults the listen address to ':7890' (all interfaces); habitat/internal/server/server.go:113-129 registers every route without an authentication layer, including POST /api/tasks/retry (server.go:121, handlers.go:960-1069) which calls absurd.retry_task. docs/tools/habitat.md:22 and habitat/README.md:23 say the dashboard is at localhost, and docs/tools/habitat.md:87 calls it a read-only view.
gaps.impact: Confidentiality and integrity: any peer that can reach the port can read task params, checkpoint states, results and event payloads, and can retry or respawn failed tasks. Operators who trust the docs can expose it unknowingly.
gaps.fix: Bind to 127.0.0.1 by default, make write endpoints opt-in (for example --allow-writes) with an Origin and content-type check, add optional token authentication, correct the docs, and test the default bind and the disabled write path.

gaps.title: Release pipeline: tag-pinned actions, publishing not gated on tests, unattested binaries
gaps.case: 0 of 37 third-party action references are SHA-pinned (probe ci.pinned_actions), two use a branch (build.yml:353, 388); test.yml and build.yml have no top-level permissions; the release job needs only build-habitat and validate-release-versions (build.yml:129) while tests live in a separate workflow; release assets are uploaded without checksums or attestations (build.yml:181-187); the habitat UI is built with npm install (build.yml:102).
gaps.impact: Supply-chain integrity: a moved tag or branch runs inside jobs holding contents:write or id-token:write; a tag can ship artefacts whose tests failed; users cannot verify habitat or standalone absurdctl binaries.
gaps.fix: Pin actions by full SHA, set top-level 'permissions: contents: read', make release and publish jobs depend on a test job in the same workflow, publish SHA256SUMS with build-provenance attestations, and use npm ci for the UI build.

gaps.title: Migrations are applied non-atomically and bump the schema version first
gaps.case: absurdctl applies each migration through psql with ON_ERROR_STOP but without --single-transaction (absurdctl:302-342, 1813-1817); the migration files have no top-level transaction and set get_schema_version as their first statement (sql/migrations/0.5.0-0.5.1.sql:6-11, 0.4.0-0.5.0.sql:6, 0.1.1-0.2.0.sql:7). A rerun compares the recorded version with the target and stops with 'already at' (absurdctl:1742-1745).
gaps.impact: A migration that fails or is killed midway leaves a partially migrated schema that already reports the new version; the default retry path then skips the rest, so stored procedures and indexes can silently mismatch the SDKs.
gaps.fix: Apply each file with psql --single-transaction (or wrap files in begin/commit), move the version bump to the end of each migration, and run scripts/validate-psql for every migration chain in CI, plus a fault-injected migration test.

gaps.title: maxDelay is documented as a no-checkpoint watchdog but implemented as a time-to-first-start limit
gaps.case: docs/concepts.md:312, docs/sdks/typescript.md:432 and docs/sdks/go.md:727 say maxDelay cancels a task if no checkpoint is written for N seconds. sql/absurd.sql:966-968 cancels only when first_started_at is null and enqueue time exceeds max_delay, which sdks/python/tests/test_retry.py:252-271 tests and docs/patterns/deployments.md:48 describes correctly.
gaps.impact: Users and agents relying on maxDelay to stop stuck running tasks get no cancellation; such tasks keep running through claim expiry and retries.
gaps.fix: Correct the three doc sites and SDK docstrings, or add a separate no-progress policy; add a docs test for the cancellation table.

gaps.title: No security policy, private reporting channel or threat model
gaps.case: git ls-files lists no SECURITY.md (probe meta.security_policy not found); CHANGELOG.md:63 records an absurdctl SQL injection fix without an advisory; no document describes database roles or grants (sql/absurd.sql has no GRANT/REVOKE and all functions run as the caller), habitat exposure or remote SQL.
gaps.impact: Reporters have no private channel; EU CRA vulnerability-handling expectations (reporting from 11 Sep 2026) are unmet; deployers cannot tell which roles may manipulate which queues.
gaps.fix: Add SECURITY.md with a private contact (GitHub Security Advisories), response times and a trust-boundary section covering database roles, habitat and absurdctl's network fetches; publish advisories for security fixes.

gaps.title: absurdctl applies schema SQL fetched from GitHub without integrity verification
gaps.case: fetch_text() reads URLs with urlopen (absurdctl:517-519); init downloads absurd.sql for any --ref that is not bundled (absurdctl:585-606) and migrate falls back to remote discovery when local migrations are incomplete (absurdctl:1716-1730); the SQL is then executed against the database (absurdctl:1813-1817).
gaps.impact: Integrity: DDL and stored procedures installed into the user's database come from a mutable branch or tag over HTTPS with no checksum or signature, and an implicit fallback can trigger the fetch.
gaps.fix: Ship a signed manifest of SHA-256 digests for released SQL files, verify before applying, refuse non-release refs unless --allow-unverified is given, and print the digest applied.

gaps.title: Habitat tests never run in CI and declared runtimes are untested
gaps.case: Makefile:39 defines test as test-core, test-typescript, test-python and test-go; habitat has no test target and test.yml:52-53 runs only make test, so 13 habitat Go tests never run. pyproject.toml:13-21 claims Python 3.9-3.14 and package.json claims node >=18, but CI uses 3.12 (test.yml:18) and 24 (test.yml:26); every suite uses postgres:16-alpine (tests/conftest.py:155), leaving the Postgres 18 uuidv7 branch (sql/absurd.sql:2305-2307) unexecuted.
gaps.impact: Regressions in the network-facing dashboard (including the retry endpoint) and on declared Python, Node and Postgres versions ship unnoticed.
gaps.fix: Add 'cd habitat && go test ./...' to make test, and a CI matrix over Python 3.9 and 3.14, Node 18 and 24, and Postgres 14-18.

gaps.title: Every run reloads all checkpoints of its task; payloads have no size limits
gaps.case: TaskContext.create loads every committed checkpoint of the task into a Map at each run start (sdks/typescript/src/index.ts:302-319; Python __init__.py:632; Go context.go:67) through get_task_checkpoint_states (sql/absurd.sql:1647-1699). params, checkpoint state and event payload columns are unbounded jsonb (sql/absurd.sql:226, 271, 284). docs/patterns/pi-ai-agent.md:39-49 recommends one checkpoint per agent message.
gaps.impact: Long agent or batch tasks with thousands of checkpoints re-read and hold their whole history on every attempt, so memory and resume latency grow linearly with no documented ceiling.
gaps.fix: Document payload and checkpoint-count limits, load checkpoints lazily by name (get_task_checkpoint_state already exists) or in pages, and add a test at 10x the expected history size.

gaps.title: Agents must parse text output and cannot match errors by code
gaps.case: absurdctl has no JSON output mode (probe agent.json_output); dump-task prints formatted text and full JSON blobs without a size bound (absurdctl:2401-2440); 17 of the 80 SQL raise sites carry an SQLSTATE code (16 AB codes and one 40001, rg counts in sql/absurd.sql) and none of the codes are documented in docs, README, CONTRIBUTING or the skill.
gaps.impact: The skill's agent users pay unbounded tokens per dump-task and must parse tables; errors cannot be handled by stable code.
gaps.fix: Add --json and --max-bytes to list and dump commands, document an error-code table, and give the remaining raise sites stable codes.

gaps.title: Unsourced size comparison and superlative in the docs
gaps.case: docs/comparison.md:83-84 states 'Temporal's Python SDK is 170.000 lines of code, Absurd's is under 2000' and docs/comparison.md:135-137 gives DBOS 40.000 lines, without method or source; README.md:8 calls Absurd 'the simplest durable execution workflow system'. Measurement: sdks/python/src/absurd_sdk/__init__.py has 2317 physical lines (wc -l) and 1801 non-blank, non-comment, non-docstring lines (tokenizer count), so the claim holds only under an unstated rule.
gaps.impact: Readers and agents selecting tools from prose cannot verify the comparison.
gaps.fix: State the counting tool, rule, commits and date for each number, or remove the numbers.

gaps.title: Habitat task rows are mouse-only
gaps.case: habitat/ui/src/views/Tasks.tsx:792-794 expands a task through an onClick on a table row with no tabindex, role or key handler; habitat/ui/src has 10 aria or role attributes in total and no accessibility tooling (probe ui.a11y).
gaps.impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot open task details (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1).
gaps.fix: Render a disclosure button per row with aria-expanded (for example Kobalte Collapsible) and add an automated accessibility check to the UI build.

opps.title: CRA-ready releases: SECURITY.md, SBOM and attested binaries
opps.description: Absurd is distributed through npm, PyPI, GitHub Releases and Go modules with no security policy, SBOM or binary attestations. Adding them to build.yml before the EU CRA's reporting (Sep 2026) and main obligations (Dec 2027) turns a compliance gap into a selling point for an infrastructure library.

opps.title: Agent-first absurdctl: JSON output and a read-only mode
opps.description: Absurd already ships a skill that steers agents to absurdctl, but the CLI prints tables and unbounded JSON blobs. A --json mode with size limits and an enforced read-only mode would let agents inspect state cheaply and safely without prose parsing.

opps.title: Turn the skill's 'Safe operating rules' into enforced policy
opps.description: The skill lists state-changing commands agents must not run blindly (init, migrate, drop-queue, cleanup, cancel, retry, emit, spawn) only as prose. An ABSURDCTL_READONLY setting or per-command allowlist checked by absurdctl, plus a matching read-only database role in the docs, would make the rule machine-checkable.

opps.title: Content-addressed step keys as an SDK helper
opps.description: The RE4exa prototype keyed Absurd steps by sha256 of canonical arguments and stored REA's content-addressed evidence ids; after a SIGKILL it resumed with 0 repeated completed calls and the same 6 evidence ids as an uncrashed control. A ctx.step variant that derives the checkpoint name from a canonical-JSON digest would make replays of deterministic tool calls idempotent by construction for evidence tools such as rea and caveman.

opps.title: One supported durable-agent path for pi instead of a stale pattern and a parallel engine
opps.description: The same organization ships two durable-agent approaches: docs/patterns/pi-ai-agent.md shows pi agent turns as Absurd steps, while pi's packages/durable re-implements tasks, checkpoints, sleeps, retries and a crash-loop guard on SQLite/JSONL. The Absurd pattern imports @mariozechner/pi-agent-core and @mariozechner/pi-ai, whereas the current packages are @earendil-works/pi-agent-core and @earendil-works/pi-ai. A maintained adapter (pi-durable Storage or lease on Absurd, or Absurd steps driving pi-durable phases) would give one tested path.

opps.title: A shared kill-and-resume conformance harness for durable engines
opps.description: Absurd's CI simulates crashes with a fake clock; pi-durable exports storage and environment conformance kits; the RE4exa prototype has a real SIGKILL test. One extracted harness (kill at step k, resume, assert no completed step reruns and identical ids) run against absurd's three SDKs and pi-durable would publish a comparable durability number for each.

reeng.component: habitat (defaults, write endpoint, request limits, CI tests)
reeng.gain: Removes unauthenticated read and write exposure in the default configuration and puts the dashboard under test.
reeng.measure: A test asserts the default bind is 127.0.0.1 and that POST /api/tasks/retry returns 403 without opt-in; habitat's 13 Go tests run in make test on every PR.

reeng.component: absurdctl migrate and sql/migrations
reeng.gain: Atomic schema upgrades whose recorded version cannot run ahead of the applied DDL.

reeng.component: release pipeline (.github/workflows/build.yml, scripts/release.sh)

targets.name: pandacode
targets.head: cd6ae2fe0e6230264f0efe75a4759b5e0b04de70
targets.scope_notes: agent-harness: a Tauri desktop app that launches coding-agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, OpenCode, Antigravity, Grok, GLM/MiMo) as host processes and serves them app tools over a per-turn loopback MCP server. Red-line decisions: the automatic SEC-6 suspicion (4 pattern hits) is rejected because all four sit in #[cfg(test)] modules or a test file with placeholder values; SEC-7 (3), EPI-5 (2), PRV-1 (3) and PRV-3 (2) are scored above their red-line levels. gaps.title: Docs say tasks start in Ask; the code starts them in Full access
gaps.case: src-tauri/src/storage.rs:23 sets DEFAULT_PERMISSION_MODE = "full", used by src/main.ts:1505, src/main.ts:2745, src/github.ts:217, src-tauri/src/overlay.rs:50-52, src-tauri/src/lib.rs:2147 and src-tauri/src/architect/profiles.rs:305. This contradicts docs/design.md:48, docs/ipc.md:8, docs/ipc.md:28, docs/agent-tools.md:26-27 and SECURITY.md:32 ('after you grant it'); only docs/approvals.md:5-7 states the real default.
gaps.impact: Readers of the architecture and security docs believe agents ask before acting, while new tasks launch Claude with bypassPermissions and Codex with danger-full-access and skip app-tool approvals (providers.rs:2618-2630, providers.rs:1236-1241, mcp_host.rs:491). The security scope rests on a grant the user never made. Impact category: excessive agency on the user's machine and accounts.
gaps.fix: Default new tasks to ask, or require an explicit first-run choice, and keep Full access as a per-task opt-in. Update design.md, ipc.md, agent-tools.md and SECURITY.md together, and add a test that asserts the default plus a CI doc check for the stated default.

gaps.title: Imported GitHub issues become Full-access prompts without an untrusted label
gaps.case: src/github.ts:154 copies the issue body verbatim into the task description, and src/github.ts:217 creates the task with mode 'full'. References inside messages are wrapped as 'GitHub context (repository content, not instructions)' at src/github.ts:48; imported bodies are not.
gaps.impact: Text written by any issue author becomes the instruction of an agent that runs without approvals once the user starts the task. Impact category: prompt injection leading to excessive agency (OWASP LLM01, LLM06).
gaps.fix: Wrap imported issue bodies in the same untrusted-context block, start imported tasks in ask mode, and show the issue author and a third-party-text marker before the task starts.

gaps.title: Billed cloud machines can be created without approval in Full access
gaps.case: src-tauri/src/vm/tools.rs:40 (vm_manage creates Daytona, AWS EC2 or AgentCore machines) and src-tauri/src/vm/tools.rs:111; src-tauri/src/providers/mcp_host.rs:491 skips approvals in full mode except for ALWAYS_ASK = ["pandacode_cloud_cli"] (src-tauri/src/cloud/deploy.rs:25). The only guard is tool-description text asking the model to confirm.
gaps.impact: Unbounded spend in the user's connected cloud accounts from a default-mode agent loop or an injected instruction. Impact category: unbounded consumption (OWASP LLM10).
gaps.fix: Add cloud create and start actions of vm_manage to ALWAYS_ASK, add a per-task machine-count or spend cap, and cover both in the mcp_host tests.

gaps.title: The UI suite and the primary platform are outside CI
gaps.case: .github/workflows/ci.yml:26-33 and :54-58 run tsc, Node tests, release-script tests and cargo test --lib on Linux only. The 54 Playwright spec files (619 tests) never run in CI, and playwright.config.ts:18 defaults to a macOS Chrome path. releases/0.3.8.md:20 ships with 8 known failing browser tests, and --lib skips src-tauri/tests/gui_path.rs.
gaps.impact: UI regressions and macOS-only behaviour reach users unchecked at about 1.7 releases per day, and failing tests become accepted.
gaps.fix: Run Playwright in Chrome and WebKit in CI on Linux and macOS (PANDACODE_TEST_CHROME set), run the full cargo test, including integration tests, on macOS and Windows, and block release tags on red.

gaps.title: No SBOM, provenance, update bot or vulnerability scan; a signing secret is exposed to dependency installs
gaps.case: Probes ci.sbom (0 steps), ci.provenance (false), deps.update_bot (none) and ci.security_scans (none); installers are unsigned by default (docs/releasing.md:134-159); .github/workflows/release.yml:57 sets APPLE_CERTIFICATE at job level, so it is in the environment of npm ci (.github/workflows/release.yml:70).
gaps.impact: Users cannot verify who built a release or which components it contains, known-vulnerable dependencies go unnoticed, and the CRA SBOM and vulnerability-handling obligations due from December 2027 are unprepared. Impact category: supply-chain integrity.
gaps.fix: Generate CycloneDX SBOMs for npm and Cargo in release.yml, add a build-provenance attestation step, enable Dependabot or Renovate with cargo-audit and npm audit gates, move the certificate secret to the signing step only, and use npm ci --ignore-scripts where the build allows.

gaps.title: Release churn outpaces qualification, with one visible maintainer
gaps.case: website/src/data/release-dates.json lists 58 releases from 2026-09-17 to 2026-10-20 (34 days), 10 of them on 2026-09-20. The release job runs only release-script tests and a liveness probe (.github/workflows/release.yml:70-91), and installed apps update silently when idle (README.md:148-152). git log shows one author.
gaps.impact: Every installed copy absorbs lightly qualified changes automatically, and a bad release reaches all installs within hours. Continuity, including custody of the update-signing key (docs/releasing.md:45-49), depends on one person.
gaps.fix: Add stable and preview update channels, batch user-facing releases, run the full test suites in the release job, and document key custody and a second maintainer.

gaps.title: Bot Guard always-ask list is a substring denylist
gaps.case: src-tauri/src/bots/guard.rs:27-31 and :66-69 match a fixed list of literal substrings case-insensitively. docs/bots.md:50 notes that the Guard does not see bots in Full access, and docs/bots.md:91 lists a model-based reviewer as not built.
gaps.impact: Equivalent forms of listed dangerous commands arriving from remote chat channels are not recognised and fall through to ordinary rule decisions. Impact category: excessive agency from untrusted remote input.
gaps.fix: Classify parsed commands (argv tokens with normalised flags) instead of substrings, treat any shell command from a remote channel as ask unless an exact allow rule matches, and add a table-driven test of equivalent command forms.

gaps.title: Per-turn MCP bearer token is placed in process arguments
gaps.case: src-tauri/src/providers.rs:2818 and src-tauri/src/providers/warm.rs:92 pass --mcp-config with the Authorization header on the harness command line. The same project keeps GLM and MiMo keys out of argv for this reason (docs/providers.md:416).
gaps.impact: Other local users or processes that can list process arguments can read the token while a turn runs and call app tools on the loopback server. Impact category: least privilege on shared hosts.
gaps.fix: Pass the MCP configuration through a 0600 temporary file, the child's environment or stdin, and add a test that no token appears in argv.

gaps.title: Privacy disclosure omits four automatic request hosts
gaps.case: src-tauri/src/agent_updates.rs:278-306 checks registry.npmjs.org, releases.openai.com, pypi.org and storage.googleapis.com. README.md:125 and website/src/pages/privacy.astro:54 list only formulae.brew.sh, downloads.claude.ai, api.github.com and cdn.kimi.com, and CONTRIBUTING.md:106-108 requires every automatic request to be listed.
gaps.impact: Users and administrators who allowlist outbound hosts from the published table get an incomplete picture. Impact category: transparency (GDPR Art. 13).
gaps.fix: Generate the privacy table from metadata_endpoint(), or add a test that every URL in agent_updates.rs appears in README.md and privacy.astro.

gaps.title: Token-saver meter shows savings PandaCode never measured
gaps.case: src/token-saver.ts:111-115 computes the share saved from fixed per-pack constants (0.12 to 0.35), and src/token-saver-panel.ts:31 and :48 show 'about N% fewer tokens'. The usage ledger already counts tokens per reply (docs/agent-usage.md:19-22).
