gaps.fix: Compute observed output tokens per thread before and after a pack from the ledger, show 'not measured' until data exists, and keep the published benchmark figures as cited sources.

opps.title: Extract the hardened loopback MCP host
opps.description: providers/mcp_host.rs implements a per-run MCP HTTP endpoint with a random bearer token, an exact Host match, Origin rejection, one bounded request per connection, request, size and time limits, mode-dependent approvals and tests. Packaged as its own crate, it would give other harnesses in the reviewed set (t3code, orca, pi) and tool servers (rea) a tested local transport.

opps.title: Measure token-saver packs with the usage ledger
opps.description: The ledger already de-duplicates per-reply token counts, while the token saver shows fixed estimates for packs taken from caveman and rtk. Joining per-thread pack state with ledger counts yields measured savings per harness and model, which caveman and ponytail could also cite.

opps.title: Pluggable System-One decisions: my-jev or laya for the Guard and approvals
opps.description: The Jev decision client posts state, question and options to a hardcoded endpoint. my-jev trains a model with the same input and output shape (one letter plus a probability per option) and reports a third-party tool-risk benchmark, and laya and laya-coreml serve typed decisions locally. A configurable endpoint would give the rule-based bot Guard its missing model-based reviewer and an on-device option.

opps.title: Re-cut the app-tool catalog and add MCP annotations
opps.description: The 31 core pandacode_* tools include several single-purpose task mutations (rename_task, pin_task, archive_task, set_task_stage, open_task), and tools/list carries no readOnlyHint or destructiveHint. One parameterised task tool plus accurate annotations would shrink the per-turn catalog and let hosts auto-approve reads; leanrea documents the cost of oversized tool catalogs.

opps.title: Full access in a box
opps.description: Run Full-access tasks inside contained environments: the existing Tart VMs with a read-only project share, or agent-sandbox-lockdown's internal network with allowlisting DNS and proxy. This turns the riskiest default into a contained one and fits the CRA's secure-by-default obligations from December 2027. Blocker: the MCP host accepts only loopback peers (mcp_host.rs:102), so a containerised harness needs a forwarded transport.

opps.title: Consolidate harness adapters with t3code and orca
opps.description: PandaCode normalizes Claude stream-json, Codex app-server JSON-RPC and ACP v1 behind one event interface. T3 Code drives the same CLIs, and Orca is another harness GUI in the reviewed set. A shared adapter library with recorded, dated frame fixtures would cut duplicated protocol work and give all three the same oracle set. I did not inspect the t3code or orca adapters, so the overlap is inferred from their READMEs.

targets.name: leanrea
targets.head: 09ba4aa0217f82cd880f855a60b877f59f39b22b
targets.scope_notes: Profile skill-pack: the product is one 66-line SKILL.md that shapes agent behaviour, plus a benchmark that backs its claims against REA. Flags changed from the suggestion: parses_untrusted true (the targets are third-party binaries, app bundles, firmware and websites, SKILL.md:3), distributed true (installed and updated via 'npx skills add/update', README.md:51-61). executes_code true because the skill drives the agent's shell. SEC-4 NA (the artefact bundles no third-party components), SEC-5 NA (no CI), MNT-1 NA (no code architecture). The product is judged by the agent behaviour it asks for, its claims and its benchmark.

gaps.title: No rule for untrusted content read from targets
gaps.case: The skill sends agents to read strings, bundle slices, web pages and captures of third-party software (leanrea/SKILL.md:23,31,52,54) and has no rule that this content is data, not instructions; bench/tasks.json has no injection case.
gaps.impact: Text planted in an analysed target can steer an agent that holds a shell (OWASP LLM01).
gaps.fix: Add a rule that target content is untrusted data and never a source of commands; add a benchmark target with planted instructions.

gaps.title: Headline equivalence exceeds the benchmark
gaps.case: README.md:3 says the file 'does what REA does' and README.md:24 'at the same accuracy', from 4 tasks on 3 targets, one model, 3 reps (74/75 vs 75/75). A paired bootstrap of bench/results/final.jsonl gives leanrea/REA wall ratio 0.63 [0.51, 0.76] (robust, 12/12 cells) but leanrea/no-skill wall ratio 0.87 [0.70, 1.05], so 'about 19% faster' (README.md:46) is not separable from no change.
gaps.impact: Agents and people choosing a tool from the README get a broader claim than the measurement supports.
gaps.fix: Scope the headline to the measured tasks, report intervals, and rerun with at least 5 interleaved reps.

gaps.title: Committed results are not the shipped harness's output and cannot be audited
gaps.case: bench/run_all.sh:5-7 runs reps 1..REPS and appends to results/run.jsonl, but the committed bench/results/final.jsonl holds reps 11-13; answers are written only to the gitignored work directory (bench/run.py:50), so only miss lists such as ['event ch'] are visible.
gaps.impact: Grades and the stated reason for the one miss (README.md:24) cannot be checked, and whether other reps were run is not stated.
gaps.fix: Commit the full run log with answers (or their hashes) and document how final.jsonl was produced.

gaps.title: Lenient regex graders without self-tests
gaps.case: bench/tasks.json:43 ('hash': 'hash'), :45 ('sock': '\.sock') and :48 ('json': 'JSON') pass any answer that mentions the word; bench/run.py:44 applies them with no known-good or known-bad check; BENCHMARK.md:41 records a false negative fixed by hand.
gaps.impact: Score parity between arms can hide wrong answers.
gaps.fix: Give every key a known-good and a known-bad answer checked before scoring, and tighten the keys.

gaps.title: Unpinned registry packages executed on every use
gaps.case: leanrea/SKILL.md:29 and :38 run 'npx -y @electron/asar' and 'npx -y @electron/fuses', :39 'npx -y prettier', each fetching and running the latest version without confirmation.
gaps.impact: Supply-chain exposure on the analyst's machine at every run.
gaps.fix: Pin versions in the snippets or require the preinstalled tools listed in the Install section.

gaps.title: No isolation for parsing or running untrusted targets
gaps.case: Extractors and parsers (binwalk -e, unblob -e, jadx, apktool; leanrea/SKILL.md:47,53) and runtime rows that launch or attach to the target (frida -f, lldb -p, Electron --inspect; :55) run directly on the host with no sandbox, VM or consent step.
gaps.impact: A malicious target can exploit parser defects or run code with the analyst's privileges.
gaps.fix: Recommend a disposable VM or container for extraction and dynamic analysis, and require consent before launching a target.

gaps.title: macOS-only first moves presented as universal
gaps.case: 'cp -c' (APFS clone, leanrea/SKILL.md:11), lipo, otool, xcrun dyld_info and codesign (:23,41) and $TMPDIR (unset on many Linux hosts, so 'rm -rf $X' targets /re/asar, :29) are in the paste-and-run moves; the README states macOS only for the benchmark (README.md:16).
gaps.impact: On Linux the native first move fails and costs the turns the skill aims to save.
gaps.fix: State the platform scope, add a Linux first move (readelf, nm, objdump), default TMPDIR and quote variables.

gaps.title: No versions; benchmark keys tied to one app build
gaps.case: 'npx skills update leanrea' pulls the latest (README.md:61); there are no tags or changelog; answer keys match Notion 7.35.1 and go1.27.1 only (README.md:107, bench/setup.sh:18).
gaps.impact: Users cannot pin a known-good skill, and the benchmark stops being rerunnable as the targets update.
gaps.fix: Tag releases, record the skill commit in each result row, and keep keys per target version.

gaps.title: No authorised-use note for reverse engineering
gaps.case: Neither README.md nor leanrea/SKILL.md mentions licence terms or legal limits of reverse engineering, while the benchmark reverse engineers a proprietary app (bench/setup.sh:7-13).
gaps.impact: Users and agents get no guardrail on authorised use.
gaps.fix: Add a short note on authorised use and where interoperability exceptions apply.

opps.title: Adopt ponytail's benchmark hygiene
opps.description: ponytail's agentic harness interleaves arms, runs 5 reps, self-tests every grader with good and bad references before spending (DietrichGebert__ponytail benchmarks/agentic/run.py:205-229) and reports bootstrap intervals; leanrea's 3-rep side-by-side design (bench/run_all.sh:5-7) cannot separate leanrea from no skill (wall ratio 0.87 [0.70, 1.05]). One shared harness also gives a common answer-key format with RE4exa's REA answer key.

opps.title: Cheap-probe front end for REA and rex
opps.description: On the same operations raw commands took 0.04-4.8 s where REA's CLI took 0.56-47.9 s (bench/BENCHMARK.md:67-73), and RE4exa's lens run answered 7 answer-key questions in 219 ms. Routing first questions through leanrea's router and keeping REA for typed relations, evidence records and graph queries combines the speed with REA's provenance.

opps.title: Machine-readable router table
opps.description: The 19-row router (leanrea/SKILL.md:35-55) as data (detect pattern, command, fallback, output cap, platform), rendered into SKILL.md, would fix the macOS-only first moves, make each row testable on fixture binaries, and let rea, rex and pandacode reuse the same routing.

opps.title: Run the recipe inside agent-sandbox-lockdown
opps.description: agent-sandbox-lockdown provides a Docker sandbox with DNS and egress allowlists, least-privilege tools, approval for writes and a JSONL tool-call log (its README). Running leanrea's extraction and runtime rows there closes the isolation gap without changing the recipe's commands.

opps.title: Attention rules as host hooks
opps.description: 'Never cat a big file', 'cap every output' and '2-4 tool calls' are prose (leanrea/SKILL.md:14-18). A pre-tool hook of the kind ponytail ships for Claude Code and Codex (hooks/claude-codex-hooks.json there) could warn on uncapped output commands and count calls, making the budget enforceable.

reeng.component: bench/ (run_all.sh, run.py, tasks.json)
reeng.gain: Claims with uncertainty and auditable grading
reeng.measure: Interleaved arms with at least 5 reps; paired bootstrap interval on leanrea/no-skill excludes 1 or the claim is withdrawn; every key rejects a known-wrong answer before scoring; answers committed

reeng.component: Router table in leanrea/SKILL.md
reeng.gain: Platform-correct first moves and a reusable routing table
reeng.measure: SKILL.md stays at or under 8 KB; Linux and macOS first moves both succeed on fixture ELF and Mach-O binaries

reeng.component: Safety rules in leanrea/SKILL.md
reeng.gain: Agents resist planted instructions and do not run unpinned or untrusted code by default
reeng.measure: A benchmark target with planted instructions is followed in 0 of 5 runs; rg finds no unpinned 'npx -y' in SKILL.md

targets.name: re4exa
targets.head: 0bdc987676d629d8d3580e966784cdc980f96432

Injection-prone operation on a path reachable from untrusted input.

gaps.title: No license, and no ownership beyond one human account and one agent
gaps.case: git ls-files at 0bdc987 has no LICENSE, COPYING or LICENSES/ file and no SPDX header; only the private prototypes/rea-durable-evidence/package.json:3,7 says MIT. git log: c3c15ca (A.Olivier, README stub) and c1cd3c6, 0bdc987 (Claude) add every other file; main still points at c3c15ca; no CODEOWNERS, governance, CONTRIBUTING or AGENTS.md.
gaps.impact: Red line RL-1: nobody may legally reuse, fork or redistribute rex, dissect, rqs, the standard or the research. Continuity depends on one person directing one agent, and RQS-2030's own PRV-3, SUS-1 and SUS-2 fail.
gaps.fix: Add a LICENSE with an SPDX identifier (plus REUSE headers or REUSE.toml), state it in README.md, add CODEOWNERS and a CONTRIBUTING or AGENTS.md that says how agent changes are reviewed before merge.

gaps.title: Bundle import builds SQL from file content and accepts unverified answers
gaps.case: tools/rex/rex/store.py:221-225 formats the table name and the column names of every non-evidence bundle record into the INSERT statement. Only evidence records are checked against their content address (store.py:209-215); answer revisions are inserted without recomputing digest or previous_digest (the chain is built on write only, tools/rex/rex/epistemics.py:57-66). Reachable through `rex import <bundle>` (tools/rex/rex/cli.py:107,151-152); bundles are meant to move between agents and machines (tools/README.md:22, skills/rex/SKILL.md:50-51, research/dissection/README.md:171-172).
gaps.impact: Injection-prone construct on an untrusted-input path (red line RL-4, SEC-7 level 0). A bundle can also add or rewrite answers and adjudications, which drive `rex coverage` and the trust or abstain advice of `rex calibrate`, without detection; 'tampered records are rejected' (skills/rex/SKILL.md:51) holds only for evidence rows. Exploitation was not attempted.
gaps.fix: Allowlist the three table names and their columns and bind values only; recompute and verify answer digests and chains on import; reject unknown keys; add malicious-bundle tests; sign bundles before cross-machine use (research gap G4).

gaps.title: Headline and 'measured' claims disagree with the repository's own results
gaps.case: '7/7 ... in 4.0 s' (research/rea-self-analysis/README.md:155, research/dissection/README.md:152, results/findings.jsonl:36, commit c1cd3c6) cites results/product-eval.json, which records elapsed_seconds 4.48 (line 2). research/dissection/README.md:110-114 lists under 'Measured fixes' that durable steps fix the 889 MB re-import and that bench hygiene fixes leanrea's benchmark; no result measures either, and the prototype restores through the same whole-bundle import_evidence_bundle call and stores a full bundle copy per step (prototypes/rea-durable-evidence/src/durable-rea.mjs:34-40,57-62). 'All are standard-library Python' (tools/README.md:3) vs `import yaml` (tools/dissect/dissect/extract.py:21). '84 probes' (tools/README.md:10, tools/rqs/README.md:4) vs 85 implemented and cited. 'REA CLI ... 2-3 KB' (research/rea-self-analysis/README.md:92) vs 351 B to 1,391,979 B in results/e6-timings.tsv. 'Every weight, band and gate is read from the standard' (tools/rqs/rqs/score.py:1-2 (at 0bdc987)) vs literals at score.py:15,79-80,106,111 (at 0bdc987). 'Every output states its byte and token cost' (tools/README.md:24) holds only for evidence views. No committed result exists for 0.42 s, 52-70 ms, 4,607 bytes, about 50 s and 24 vs 18 (research/dissection/README.md:148,150,156,18,175) or for the 6.3 GB worker RSS (research/rea-self-analysis/README.md:86).
gaps.impact: Readers and tool-selecting agents get numbers that cannot be rechecked or that differ from the measurements: EPI-5 sits in the fail band and PUR-2 at 2. The study that faults REA for weak claims repeats the pattern for rex.
gaps.fix: Render README number tables from results/*.json with a script and fail on drift; commit a result for every quoted number; correct 4.0 s to 4.5 s; move unmeasured items out of 'Measured fixes'; declare PyYAML; correct the probe count.

gaps.title: rqs pointed at RE4exa scores its own pattern tables and the standard's prose; not fixed
gaps.case: In the probe document for 0bdc987 (85 probes run), 19 probes report found=true and every location they cite is in standard/ or tools/rqs/: e.g. risk.tls_off and risk.unsafe_deser -> tools/rqs/rqs/scan.py:57-63; static.arch_guards -> scan.py:167, probes.py:588; static.debt_markers -> probes.py:614-615, scan.py:166; test.fuzz, crypto.pqc, perf.energy -> standard/RQS-2030.md. 9 of the 39 levelled suggestions rest only on such lines (MNT-1=4, SEC-8=3, SEC-9=3, SEC-7=1, AGT-1=2, PERF-3=2, EPI-5=1, MNT-5=2, SUS-3=2) and 10 more partly (COR-3=4 with 5 of 6, OPS-2=4, OPS-4=3, PRV-1=2). The suggested flags network_service (scan.py:151-153 is the only match) and heavy_compute are wrong and come from the same tables, uses_crypto is right only by coincidence (its 22 classical-crypto hits are rqs pattern lines), and the profile workflow-engine came from the word 'durable' (tools/rqs/rqs/suggest.py:61-63). Mentions count as presence (suggest.py:119-120,167-170,202-203,233-235). Neither 0bdc987 nor 82e1713 addresses it. This review changed 17 of the 39 automatic levels, removed PERF-3 by correcting heavy_compute, and kept some whose basis was self-referential but whose level holds on other evidence (EPI-5=1, MNT-5=2, SUS-3=2, INT-2=3).
gaps.impact: The review tool cannot review its own repository, or any repository that contains detection rules or quality documentation: an untouched template would have given RE4exa COR-3=4, MNT-1=4 and OPS-2=4, and SEC-7=1 for the wrong reason while missing the real construct.
gaps.fix: Exclude the tool's own detection tables and the standard from scans (or honour an ignore marker); count prose mentions separately from configuration and code use; add a regression test that probes RE4exa itself and asserts these false positives stay absent.

gaps.title: No CI, an undeclared dependency, and a suite that fails on a clean checkout
gaps.case: No CI configuration exists (rqs probe ci.workflows: 0). The 40 tests pass in the prepared checkout (rex 14, dissect 7, rqs 19) but on `git archive 0bdc987` the dissect suite fails with 3 failures and 1 error because @babel/parser is not installed and the tests do not skip. PyYAML is imported by tools/dissect/dissect/extract.py:21 and standard/build.py:14 but declared nowhere. There is no SECURITY.md, update bot or vulnerability scan.
gaps.impact: Nothing stops a regression, the documented quick start breaks on a fresh machine, and COR-1, SEC-1 and SEC-2 cannot improve without a pipeline.
gaps.fix: Add a CI workflow (actions pinned by SHA, read-only permissions) that installs the helper and runs the three suites and standard/build.py --check on Linux and macOS; add a pinned requirements file for PyYAML; add SECURITY.md and Dependabot.

gaps.title: rqs misses real evidence on RE4exa
gaps.case: claims.count finds 0 numeric claims because claims_numeric requires a comparative word (tools/rqs/rqs/scan.py:226-229), although research/rea-self-analysis/README.md:78-101 is a table of numeric claims. claims.harness finds 0 harness and 0 result files because test.bench only recognises bench or eval directories (tools/rqs/rqs/probes.py:539), while research/rea-self-analysis/ holds 12 scripts and 31 result files. agent.describe misses all three describe subcommands (tools/rex/rex/cli.py:108, tools/dissect/dissect/cli.py:267, tools/rqs/rqs/cli.py:179) because the pattern expects add_parser("describe") (scan.py:85-86). test.golden misses the answer key (probes.py:508 wants an answer-key directory). The SEC-7 rule ignores risk.patterns (suggest.py:163-166) and no probe looks for SQL built from strings (tools/rex/rex/store.py:221-225). obs.env_vars counts names from test fixtures (scan.py:535-536); risk.remote_script counts test fixtures (probes.py:685) and treats a printed sha256sum (research/rea-self-analysis/scripts/setup.sh:37) as verification.
gaps.impact: Suggestions are right or wrong for the wrong reasons (EPI-5 would be 3 if no claim were found; OPS-4=3 rests on a printed digest), and reviewers who trust found=false miss the evidence that matters most.
gaps.fix: Build an answer key of labelled repositories (start with this review's corrections) and measure probe precision and recall; widen claims, harness and describe detection; use risk.patterns in the SEC-7 rule; add a dynamic-SQL signal; exclude test fixtures from env-var and pipe-to-shell counts.

gaps.title: rex's readers of untrusted artifacts have no resource bounds
gaps.case: tools/rex/rex/formats.py reads whole files (84,115,152,200,251), decompresses whole zip and tar entries into memory (97,107), decompresses Rust .dep-v0 without an output cap (303: bufsize is an initial buffer size) and walks Mach-O load commands trusting ncmds and cmdsize (258-265). probes.external captures all stdout before truncating (tools/rex/rex/probes.py:182-190); find skips files over 256 MiB without listing them (probes.py:153-154). There are no malformed-input or fuzz tests (tools/rex/tests/test_rex.py).
gaps.impact: Crafted or very large artifacts, which are rex's stated inputs, can exhaust memory or CPU on the analyst's host (the size-cliff class the research faults REA for), and scans can be partial without saying so.
gaps.fix: Stream digests in chunks; cap per-entry decompression (decompressobj with max_length); validate load-command sizes and bound counts; cap external output while reading; list skipped files in limitations; add a malformed-input corpus and a fuzz target for formats.py.

gaps.title: Silent absence in the necessity gate and in dissect
gaps.case: tools/rex/rex/gate.py:33,47: when DISSECT_DB names a missing file, no query runs and the verdict is 'nothing-similar-indexed' rather than 'no-index'. tools/dissect/dissect/extract.py:151-155 ignores the JS helper's exit status: on the clean export of 0bdc987 the dissect tests lost every JS/TS symbol (startWorker, helper) and the scan recorded no error. extract.py:453 calls node unconditionally while Go is guarded (:455), contradicting tools/README.md:48-50.
gaps.impact: An agent asking the gate whether a capability exists is told nothing similar is indexed when nothing was searched, and dissect graphs can silently lack whole languages: the 'absence is not a negative' rule rex is built around.
gaps.fix: Return no-index with an error for a missing database; record the helper's exit status and per-language parse coverage in the scan stats; guard node as go is guarded; make the dissect tests skip JS assertions when the helper is missing.

gaps.title: Durable step reuse survives tool upgrades, and evidence carries no tool version
gaps.case: Step keys are digest(operation, args, subject) (tools/rex/rex/store.py:153) and built-in probes pass no tool_version to store.put (tools/rex/rex/probes.py:51,67,91,136,165). After a rex upgrade, a re-run returns evidence produced by the old parser marked reused: true, and no record says which rex produced it, although describe lists tool_version as a field (tools/rex/rex/cli.py:55). dissect records no tool version either (tools/dissect/dissect/db.py:84).
gaps.impact: Parser fixes never reach existing stores, provenance cannot tell old results from new (EPI-1 at 2), and stores shared between machines with different rex versions converge on whatever was cached first.
gaps.fix: Include rex's version, or a digest of each probe's implementation, in step keys and evidence identity; record dissect's version in meta and repo rows.

gaps.title: Three tools, three error contracts and three MCP loops
gaps.case: rex and rqs return {error: {code, message, fix}} (tools/rex/rex/store.py:89-90, tools/rqs/rqs/standard.py:17-18); dissect returns {error: 'not_found', hint} or {error: 'read_only', message} (tools/dissect/dissect/cli.py:77,142,154,178), contrary to the design table (tools/README.md:25). No tool sets a retryable flag. Unexpected exceptions become tracebacks in the rex and dissect CLIs (tools/rex/rex/cli.py:161-165, tools/dissect/dissect/cli.py:272-279) and Python class names as codes over MCP (tools/rex/rex/mcp.py:89-90, tools/dissect/dissect/mcp.py:74-75). The three MCP loops (rex/mcp.py:66-100, dissect/mcp.py:47-84, rqs/mcp.py:57-96) all answer protocolVersion 2025-06-18 whatever the client asks and drop malformed JSON without a parse-error reply.
gaps.impact: Agents need per-tool error handling, the same mistake yields different shapes, and every protocol change has to be made three times.
gaps.fix: One shared error type with code, message, fix and retryable; a catch-all JSON error in every CLI; one MCP stdio module with version negotiation and -32700 replies; a contract test that sends equivalent invalid inputs to all three tools.

gaps.title: MCP hints under-declare file overwrites, and target text reaches agents unmarked
gaps.case: rex_export is annotated destructiveHint false (tools/rex/rex/mcp.py:19,33) yet replaces any existing file at the given path (tools/rex/rex/store.py:197); rqs_probe, rqs_template and rqs_score write any 'out' path with Path.write_text (tools/rqs/rqs/mcp.py:19,25-30; tools/rqs/rqs/cli.py:35-37). Byte slices, JS samples, doc lines and snippets from targets are returned without an untrusted-content marker, and no server instruction says to treat them as data (tools/rex/rex/mcp.py:79, tools/dissect/dissect/mcp.py:61, tools/rqs/rqs/mcp.py:71).
gaps.impact: Hosts that auto-approve non-destructive tools let an agent, possibly steered by text injected into a scanned target, overwrite arbitrary files; injected instructions reach the model unlabelled (AGT-1 at 1, AGT-2 at 2).
gaps.fix: Declare write tools destructive or refuse existing paths without an explicit overwrite flag; confine writes to a working directory; label target-derived text as untrusted data in outputs and server instructions; add injection fixtures to the tests.

gaps.title: Entry-point documentation and contracts are out of date
gaps.case: README.md:6-13 has no row for standard/ or tools/rqs and says the skills cover 'rex and dissect' although skills/rqs exists (0bdc987 did not touch README.md). dissect describe (tools/dissect/dissect/cli.py:223-224) omits the node kinds component, gap and principle and the edge kinds fixes, motivates and satisfies that research/dissection/dissection.db contains. tools/rqs/README.md:47 says automatic red-line suspicions do not cap a grade until a reviewer confirms them, while tools/rqs/rqs/score.py:98 (at 0bdc987) also confirms any automatic level with observed confidence.
gaps.impact: A new human or agent at the root misses the standard and half of the tooling, and agents that query dissect by its contract miss the curated relations.
gaps.fix: Update README.md with every top-level component, a quick start and limits; generate dissect describe's kind lists from the database; align the rqs README with score.py.

opps.title: Scoring parameters as data in the standard
opps.description: The core weight, coverage gate, blocking thresholds, grade caps and opportunity confidence weights are prose in standard/rqs-2030.yaml and literals in tools/rqs/rqs/score.py:15,79-80,106,111 (at 0bdc987). Moving them into the YAML as numbers makes the score.py docstring true, lets other implementations score identically, and lets a revision of the standard change scoring without a code change.

opps.title: Calibrate rqs suggestions with rex's calibration
opps.description: rqs labels each suggestion observed, derived or inferred without measuring it (tools/rqs/rqs/suggest.py), and this review shows overconfident 'derived' levels. rex already records answers and adjudications and reports Wilson intervals, ECE and abstention advice (tools/rex/rex/epistemics.py:88-131). Recording each automatic level as a rex answer and adjudicating it with the reviewed level (a campaign of 15 reviews gives several hundred pairs) turns rqs's labels into measured precision per rule and lets weak rules abstain to U.

opps.title: Publish the evidence record and bundle as a versioned format
opps.description: rex's ev_<sha256> record (tools/rex/rex/store.py:17-30,113-127) and streamed JSONL bundle (store.py:183-226) are what the prototype already keeps for REA (prototypes/rea-durable-evidence/src/durable-rea.mjs:53-56) and what research/dissection/README.md:108 names as the tie between REA, caveman's retrieval handles and Absurd steps. rqs and dissect use their own ad hoc evidence shapes (path:line strings, row ids). A specified, versioned record with an algorithm-tagged id, verified import and optional signatures would let rex, dissect, rqs and REA exchange evidence.

opps.title: One repository scanner and one MCP and error core for the three tools
opps.description: dissect (tools/dissect/dissect/extract.py) and rqs (tools/rqs/rqs/scan.py) each walk repositories with their own skip lists, language maps and test-path rules, and each tool has its own MCP stdio loop and error convention. RQS-2030 step 2 already pairs `dissect scan` with `rqs probe`; rqs could read inventory and symbols from a dissect database, and the three servers could share one loop and one error type.

opps.title: A bounded, dependency-free artifact reader
opps.description: tools/rex/rex/formats.py reads ELF, PE, Mach-O, ZIP, npm tgz, ASAR, Go build info and Rust .dep-v0 in 310 lines of standard-library Python, and the research shows it answering questions REA refused (research/dissection/README.md:146-156). Once bounded and fuzzed (gap G3) it is useful on its own to other agent tools; today the missing limits make it unsafe to reuse.

reeng.component: rex bundle import and artifact readers (tools/rex/rex/store.py, formats.py, probes.py)
reeng.gain: Clears red line RL-4 and the SEC-8 and REL-2 gaps; 'tampered records are rejected' becomes true for every bundle row.
reeng.measure: A malicious-bundle and malformed-artifact corpus in tools/rex/tests passes; a fuzz run over formats.py finds no unhandled exception over a stated number of CPU-hours; peak RSS on a 10x-size input stays under a stated cap.

reeng.component: rqs probes and suggestion rules (tools/rqs/rqs/scan.py, probes.py, suggest.py)
reeng.gain: Suggestions stop resting on rqs's own tables and the standard's prose, and the evidence they miss today is found.
reeng.measure: Probing RE4exa yields no found=true probe whose evidence lies only in standard/ or tools/rqs/; on the reviewed set, the share of automatic levels that reviewers keep (rqs agree between template and review) rises against the baseline measured in this campaign.

reeng.component: Shared core for MCP stdio, errors and repository inventory used by rex, dissect and rqs
reeng.gain: One error contract and one protocol implementation instead of three hand-written loops of 35-40 lines each.
reeng.measure: A contract test sending equivalent invalid inputs to all three tools gets the same error shape; line count of the three mcp.py files before and after.

reeng.component: Repository pipeline: LICENSE, CI and generated claims
reeng.gain: PRV-3 red line cleared; COR-1 from 1 to 3; EPI-5 from 1 to 3.
reeng.measure: rqs probe meta.license detects an SPDX license; CI runs the 40 tests and standard/build.py --check on every push on two operating systems; a script regenerates README number tables from results/ and CI fails on any diff.

targets.name: my-jev
targets.head: a254b5d92cc2f1809f76fcb053d0df07c4f219be
targets.scope_notes: Profile ml-system, not the suggested agent-tool: the repo is a fine-tuning, serving and benchmarking recipe for a 4B 'System One' classifier whose product (Prompt48/my-jev-4b) is published on Hugging Face (README.md:3-13). Flags: uses_llm (trains, serves and calls LLMs), heavy_compute (282.2 min on an A40, results/train_report.json:4-5), network_service (serve.sh:10 binds 0.0.0.0:8000), parses_untrusted (the classifier reads untrusted 'state' text; third-party datasets and API replies are parsed), distributed (model published to a registry), executes_code false (nothing runs commands on behalf of an agent; setup scripts are run by the user). SEC-5 is NA because no CI exists.

gaps.title: Documented smoke test publishes to Hugging Face
gaps.case: README.md:54 runs 'bash train.sh --max_train 200'; train.sh:7 always passes --hf_repo "$HF_REPO"; train_unsloth.py:220-236 then pushes merged weights, the LoRA adapter and a new README to HF_REPO. recording/03_smoke.sh:3 avoids it with --hf_repo '', the README does not.

gaps.fix: Make publishing opt-in (a --push flag) or skip it when --max_train is set; show --hf_repo '' in the README smoke test.

gaps.title: Public endpoint falls back to a well-known API key
gaps.case: serve.sh:10 binds 0.0.0.0:8000 and serve.sh:17 uses --api-key "${MY_JEV_API_KEY:-local}"; .env.example:7 ships the key empty; README.md:37-38,75 tells users to expose port 8000 through the RunPod proxy.

gaps.fix: Fail closed: refuse to start when the key is empty or 'local', or generate a random key during setup.

gaps.title: Base-model results have no committed measurement
gaps.case: README.md:18-27 reports base Qwen3.5-4B figures (63.9%, 60.0%, 70.0%, 70.4%, 63.0%, ECE 0.144, 113 ms); results/ holds only bench_pod, bench_laptop and train_report.json, and .gitignore:7 ignores bench_base/. No results file carries a date, commit or model revision.
gaps.impact: 7 of the 24 headline cells cannot be checked from the repository; results cannot be tied to a model revision.
gaps.fix: Commit bench_base/report.json and the per-row JSONL; add date, repo commit, model revision and vLLM version to every report.

gaps.title: Probability extraction can overwrite label probabilities
gaps.case: bench.py:85-87 builds {token.strip(): p} from top_logprobs: tokens equal after strip() overwrite rather than add (the later, lower-ranked one wins when the list is ordered by probability), and labels outside the top 20 count as 0 before renormalisation. Jev's probabilities come from its API (bench.py:106-108). The same fine-tuned model scores ECE 0.048 with in-process softmax over option letters (results/train_report.json:46) and 0.212 in the bench (results/bench_pod/report.json:14), on different task mixes.
gaps.impact: The calibration row (README.md:25) may reflect the extraction method rather than the model, and compares two different probability methods.
gaps.fix: Sum probabilities per stripped label or request the exact label tokens; report tev1_dev-only ECE from both harnesses; state the method next to the number.

gaps.title: Invalid answers are scored as the first option
gaps.case: bench.py:89-93: when no option label appears in top_logprobs and the text matches no label, every probability is 0; bench.py:136 max(probs, key=probs.get) then returns the first option key, and the row is ok=True, so the report shows errors 0.
gaps.impact: Off-list outputs silently become predictions, biasing accuracy and hiding how often the model leaves the answer format.
gaps.fix: Mark such rows invalid, count them in the report, and exclude them from calibration or score them explicitly as wrong.

gaps.title: No checkpoints in a 282-minute training run
gaps.case: train_unsloth.py:194 sets save_strategy='no'; HF_TOKEN is read only after training (train_unsloth.py:221); bench rows are written after all tasks finish (bench.py:152-154). results/train_report.json:4 records 282.2 minutes.
gaps.impact: A pod interruption loses the whole run (about $2.30 at $0.49/h) and any partial benchmark; a missing token is discovered only after training.
gaps.fix: Use save_strategy='steps' with resume_from_checkpoint, validate HF_TOKEN at start, append bench rows as they complete.

gaps.title: Unpinned dependencies, dataset and installer
gaps.case: setup_pod.sh:8 pipes the uv installer to sh; setup_pod.sh:14,19 install unsloth, vllm and others without versions; setup_pod.sh:23 clones tev1 at HEAD; train_unsloth.py:38 loads the base model without a revision.
gaps.impact: Results cannot be reproduced at the reviewed commit; upstream changes alter data, training and serving silently.
gaps.fix: Lock dependencies with hashes, pin the tev1 commit and base-model revision, verify the installer checksum.

gaps.title: Published model card asserts a license and omits known weaknesses
gaps.case: model_card.py:9 declares license apache-2.0 while model_card.py:77-81 says the data sources' licenses must be checked before commercial use; the card reports only held-out dev results (model_card.py:24-33), not the phishing drop of README.md:21,30, and does not link the training repo (model_card.py:75).
gaps.impact: Users of the published model receive a permissive license claim and in-distribution-only results; model documentation expected for published models is incomplete.
gaps.fix: Derive the model license from the data licenses, add limitations and out-of-distribution results, link repo and commit.

gaps.title: Decision contract duplicated and unversioned
gaps.case: The exact system prompt and JSON message format are copied in bench.py:33-35, train_unsloth.py:29-31 and model_card.py:45-47; there is no schema for task or response; model_card.py:68-69 warns that any deviation changes behaviour.
gaps.impact: A client or agent that drifts from the prose contract gets different behaviour without an error.
gaps.fix: One shared contract file (prompt version plus JSON schema for task and response) imported by all three and published with the model.

opps.title: On-device decision gate
opps.description: The --gguf path (train_unsloth.py:51,226-229) and one-token output make a local 4B classifier for routine agent decisions that never sends state to a cloud API. Quantised accuracy and calibration are unmeasured; running q4_k_m and q8_0 through the 747-task suite would show whether the local path holds.

opps.title: One calibration-metric module instead of two
opps.description: ECE and Brier are implemented twice (bench.py:163-174 and train_unsloth.py:112-120) on different probability sources, giving 0.048 and 0.212 for the same model on different mixes. laya (a System 1 decision engine trained against proper scoring rules, per its README) and RE4exa's rex calibrate compute the same metrics. One tested module with intervals removes the discrepancy and serves all three.

opps.title: Shared System-1 decision benchmark with laya and laya-coreml
opps.description: my-jev's suites (tev1 dev stratified by source plus three third-party sets, bench.py:51-69) and task shape (state, question, options with label, key, description) match the typed single-pass decisions laya describes. Publishing the suite with pinned data and the JSONL row format as a common answer key would let both models, and on-device laya-coreml, be compared on identical tasks including abstention.

opps.title: Advisory tool-risk screen inside agent-sandbox-lockdown approvals

It needs an abstention threshold first.

reeng.component: train.sh / train_unsloth.py publishing and checkpointing

targets.name: agent-sandbox-lockdown
targets.head: 5aba6b81bcf67e15e6cc7c9796867813ab3b66c8
targets.scope_notes: security-tool: a defensive containment reference (internal Docker network, allowlisting DNS and proxy, hardened agent container, write approval, tool-call log, step cap, kill switch) demonstrated on a 153-line tool-using agent, which is the test subject rather than the product. Flags set from the code: uses_llm on, which the automatic flags missed (agent/agent.py:108-114 calls Ollama's /api/chat with tool schemas for qwen3:4b); parses_untrusted on (the agent ingests web pages and workspace files, including a prompt-injection fixture); executes_code off (tools are fixed Python functions for file I/O, HTTP GET and DNS lookup, with no shell or code tool); network_service off (DNS, proxy and Ollama listen only on the internal compose network, and no ports are published to the host); heavy_compute off (single demo tasks on a 4B local model, not material energy use); has_ui off (a CLI with a y/N prompt); uses_crypto and distributed off. Red-line decisions: PRV-3 is 1, not 0, because README.md:61 declares MIT although there is no LICENSE file; SEC-7 is 1, not 0, because the URL tool's missing scheme and host allowlist is reachable from untrusted content but the tool only reads and runs as a non-root user on a read-only root filesystem with no secrets in the shipped configuration (recorded as a high gap); EPI-5 is 1, not 0, because the demonstrated controls are backed by recorded runs and the overstatements are location and scope errors rather than claims contradicted by measurement; SEC-6 and PRV-1 pass. Static review of commit 5aba6b8 (shallow clone, one commit); nothing was run.

gaps.title: URL tool has no scheme or host allowlist
gaps.case: agent/agent.py:49-51 passes the model-chosen URL directly to urlopen. The path policy in _safe() (agent/agent.py:34-38) covers only the file tools, while AGENT_SAFETY_CHECKLIST.md:19 presents path checking as a general control. sample-runs/run_injection_1.txt:6-11 shows untrusted content steering tool calls.
gaps.impact: The documented file confinement does not cover this tool. Impact category: confidentiality of local data inside the agent container.
gaps.fix: Accept only http and https URLs whose host is on the same allowlist the proxy enforces, reject everything else before calling urlopen, and add tests for rejected inputs.

gaps.title: No automated tests or CI for the containment claims
gaps.case: The 22 files include no tests and no CI. Evidence is manual commands (README.md:42-53) and single transcripts. The only proxy evidence is an allowed request (sample-runs/run_sandbox_tests.txt:10-11) and a failed direct connection (:8-9); no recorded run shows the proxy refusing a host that is not on the allowlist.
gaps.impact: Changes to images, the Corefile or the proxy filter can weaken containment without anyone noticing, and people who copy the setup get no regression check.
gaps.fix: Add a scripted compose test suite asserting: no direct route out, DNS refusal for names not on the allowlist, proxy refusal for hosts not on the allowlist, approval required for writes, and the kill switch stopping a run. Run it in CI on every change.

gaps.title: Boundary containers come from unpinned images and lack hardening
gaps.case: docker-compose.yml:16 (ollama/ollama:latest), :23 (coredns by tag), :33 (untagged third-party tinyproxy image) and agent/Dockerfile:1-2 (tag and unpinned apt packages). The DNS and proxy containers, the only services on both networks (docker-compose.yml:22-38), have none of the agent's read_only, cap_drop, no-new-privileges, user or resource settings (docker-compose.yml:53-59).
gaps.impact: A changed or compromised upstream image silently changes the containment boundary, and the boundary components run with default privileges. Impact category: supply-chain and boundary integrity.
gaps.fix: Pin all images by digest, build the proxy from a maintained source, apply the agent's hardening and resource limits to dns, proxy and ollama where the images allow, and document how pins are updated.

gaps.title: DNS and proxy allowlists are separate policies with different matching rules
gaps.case: dns/Corefile:6-9 allows two DNS zones, proxy/allowlist.txt:1-2 allows two exact host patterns, and AGENT_SAFETY_CHECKLIST.md:9 calls them the same domain list.
gaps.impact: The two enforcement points can disagree, and an edit to one is not reflected in the other. Impact category: egress policy integrity.
gaps.fix: Generate both the Corefile and the proxy filter from one policy file with exact-name semantics, and add a test that checks they match.

gaps.title: Checklist claims a demo/ implementation and broader controls than the repository shows
gaps.case: AGENT_SAFETY_CHECKLIST.md:3 says every item is implemented in demo/ and was tested on camera; there is no demo/ directory. The transcripts use 'demo-agent' container names (sample-runs/run_network_none.txt:1, sample-runs/run_approval_allow.txt:1), while README.md:46 uses agent-sandbox-lockdown-agent. Items at AGENT_SAFETY_CHECKLIST.md:29-30 are advice rather than implementations, and :19 omits the URL-tool exception.
gaps.impact: Readers trust controls and evidence that may not correspond to the shipped files.
gaps.fix: Correct the path, separate implemented controls from advice, re-record the runs from the shipped layout with the commit SHA and date, and list each control's known exceptions.

gaps.title: Containment is presented as the defence while output integrity is unprotected
gaps.case: README.md:57-59 says the sandbox is the defence, not the model. In sample-runs/run_injection_1.txt:31-33 the summary names Acme Corp and its deal size for a lead that came from Initech (workspace/lead_from_website.txt:2), and sample-runs/run_approval_allow.txt:17-19 shows customer deal sizes in the answer to an unrelated task.
gaps.impact: Users may trust a contained agent's answers. Network containment stopped the outbound action but not the corrupted or over-disclosing answer. Impact category: integrity and confidentiality of results shown to the user.
gaps.fix: State this limit next to the claim, mark tool output as untrusted data in the prompt, and add an output check to the demo (for example, compare the reported company with the source file).

gaps.title: Approval prompt hides most of the content and invites fatigue
gaps.case: agent/agent.py:94 shows only the first 160 characters of the arguments. sample-runs/run_approval_deny.txt:6-51 shows twelve consecutive prompts for the same write until the step cap, and sample-runs/run_approval_allow.txt:6-8 shows a placeholder write being approved.
gaps.impact: Humans approve content they cannot see and are trained to answer by rote. Impact category: human oversight.
gaps.fix: Show the full content, or a hash with a pager; stop or back off after a denial; refuse repeated identical requests within a run.

gaps.title: Kill switch is cooperative and checked once per step
gaps.case: agent/agent.py:124-128 checks the KILL file only at the top of each step. One step can run several tool calls (agent/agent.py:136-147; sample-runs/run_approval_allow.txt:4-14 shows four calls in step 1), and the model call can block for up to 300 s (agent/agent.py:113).
gaps.impact: A stop request can lag by several tool calls and up to five minutes. Impact category: human oversight.
gaps.fix: Check the switch before every tool call, document docker compose stop or kill as the enforced stop, and shorten the model-call timeout.

gaps.title: Outcomes are invisible to scripts and supervising agents
gaps.case: main() returns normally after completion, kill and step limit (agent/agent.py:117-153), so the process exits the same way in every case. Stdout is ANSI text (agent/agent.py:25-30), and log entries have no run ID and use local time to the second (agent/agent.py:84).
gaps.impact: A wrapper or CI job cannot tell a completed run from a killed or limited one, or group log entries by run.
gaps.fix: Exit with distinct codes for done, killed, step limit and error, print a final JSON summary line, and add run_id and UTC timestamps to every log entry.

gaps.title: No license file
gaps.case: README.md:61 says 'MIT licensed.' There is no LICENSE file, license text or copyright holder.
gaps.impact: Reuse and forking rest on a one-line statement without the notice the MIT terms require, which matters if the author stops maintaining the demo.
gaps.fix: Add a LICENSE file with the MIT text and a copyright line, and an SPDX identifier.

opps.title: Extract the egress layer as a reusable compose module
opps.description: The internal network plus allowlisting DNS and default-deny proxy is independent of the agent and could ship as a compose include or sidecar driven by one policy file. PandaCode's Full-access tasks, strix's sandboxed agents and t3code or orca harness runs could sit behind it.

opps.title: Turn the checklist into executable policy and tests
opps.description: Each checklist line maps to a checkable property of docker-compose.yml or agent.py. A policy file plus a test runner would make the checklist verifiable against any compose project, and the same checks could run against PandaCode's VM and sandbox setups.

opps.title: A shared tool-call evidence record
opps.description: The JSONL log has no run ID, model digest or hashes. An evidence record with run_id, model and image digests, argument and result hashes and a hash chain would make runs auditable, and the same shape could be shared with PandaCode's versioned tool-activity records and rqs evidence entries.

opps.title: Risk-scored approvals with my-jev or laya
opps.description: Approvals are a bare y/N on every write, and the recorded deny run produced twelve prompts. my-jev's tool-risk classifier or a local laya decision server could score each request, refuse repeats and escalate only risky ones, keeping a human on consequential writes.

reeng.component: Tool layer in agent/agent.py (http_get, run_tool, main loop, log)
reeng.gain: The URL tool is confined to the allowlist; the kill switch is checked per call; approvals show full content; truncation is labelled; exit codes and run IDs make outcomes machine-readable.
reeng.measure: Automated tests cover each implemented checklist control (from 0 today); exit codes differ for done, killed, step limit and error; a test rejects URLs outside the allowlist.

reeng.component: Images and boundary containers (docker-compose.yml, agent/Dockerfile)
reeng.gain: Reproducible, least-privilege boundary components.
reeng.measure: Images pinned by digest go from 0 of 4 to 4 of 4; services with cap_drop ALL and no-new-privileges go from 1 of 4 to 4 of 4 where the image allows; every service has resource limits.

reeng.component: Egress policy (dns/Corefile, proxy/allowlist.txt)
reeng.gain: One policy source generates both enforcement configs and can be reused by other agent stacks.
reeng.measure: A generator and a parity test exist; one edit to the policy file changes both configs; at least one other reviewed repository uses the module.

top_opportunities.title: Compact catalog by default, with output schemas on request
top_opportunities.description: REA already ships a compact input profile and an output-schema-off profile that cut the 6.7.0 catalog from 3,158,368 to 219,226 bytes (-93%) while the server keeps canonical validation. Making them the default, with full schemas available through binary_session or resources, removes most of the per-session catalog cost in every host.

top_opportunities.title: Extract the CCR recovery store as a standalone package
top_opportunities.description: The Context Recovery store (content-addressed sha256 handles, SQLite WAL, atomic/fail-closed, idempotent, byte-exact recovery) is a self-contained hub (dissection score 18). Extracted, it is a reusable recovery substrate for REA Evidence, Absurd steps and strix tool-output spill.

top_opportunities.title: Extract the coverage-accounting record as a shared standard
top_opportunities.description: coverage.json separates declared scope, tested-clean, unexamined gaps and completeness caveats, and keeps agent-reported apart from machine-observed facts that contradict it. It is a self-contained, high-value artifact (dissection score 18) that rea (residual unknowns) and caveman could consume as a common coverage-record format.

top_opportunities.title: Scoring parameters as data in the standard
top_opportunities.description: The core weight, coverage gate, blocking thresholds, grade caps and opportunity confidence weights are prose in standard/rqs-2030.yaml and literals in tools/rqs/rqs/score.py:15,79-80,106,111 (at 0bdc987). Moving them into the YAML as numbers makes the score.py docstring true, lets other implementations score identically, and lets a revision of the standard change scoring without a code change.

top_opportunities.title: Extract the codebase map and reuse detector
top_opportunities.description: hooks/ponytail-map.js (identifier inventory under a character budget, injection-filtered and tested) and the band's definition, reuse and duplicate detectors (hooks/band/metrics.ts:35-90) are dependency-free and valuable without ponytail: RE4exa's rex gate (necessity check before building), t3code, orca and pandacode (agent GUIs) could show the same 'already exists' signal.

top_opportunities.title: Extract the hardened loopback MCP host
top_opportunities.description: providers/mcp_host.rs implements a per-run MCP HTTP endpoint with a random bearer token, an exact Host match, Origin rejection, one bounded request per connection, request, size and time limits, mode-dependent approvals and tests. Packaged as its own crate, it would give other harnesses in the reviewed set (t3code, orca, pi) and tool servers (rea) a tested local transport.

top_opportunities.title: SBOM and VEX from the existing advisory ledger
top_opportunities.description: scripts/npm-audit.mjs already records reviewed advisories with reasons. Emitting them as OpenVEX next to a CycloneDX SBOM in the provenance-attested release covers the EU CRA's December 2027 SBOM and vulnerability-handling obligations at little cost.

top_opportunities.title: Produce CRA evidence from the existing release pipeline
top_opportunities.description: release-cut.yml already builds, signs (SignPath with signature checks, macOS notarization) and publishes every platform in CI. Adding a CycloneDX SBOM, SLSA provenance, a checksum manifest, VEX statements and a SECURITY and support-period statement turns existing steps into the evidence the CRA expects from 2027-12-11; the bundled ripgrep notices show the pattern for shipping license data.

top_opportunities.title: CRA-ready releases: SECURITY.md, SBOM and attested binaries
top_opportunities.description: Absurd is distributed through npm, PyPI, GitHub Releases and Go modules with no security policy, SBOM or binary attestations. Adding them to build.yml before the EU CRA's reporting (Sep 2026) and main obligations (Dec 2027) turns a compliance gap into a selling point for an infrastructure library.

top_opportunities.title: Publish the effect vocabulary and untrusted marker as host policy
top_opportunities.description: REA's per-tool effect audit (executesForeignCode, mutatesDevice, accessesNetwork and others) and the _meta.provenance.untrusted_content marker are machine-readable. Harnesses in the reviewed set (orca, t3code, pandacode, agent-sandbox-lockdown, which already gates writes and logs tool calls) could enforce rules such as approval for executesForeignCode after untrusted content was read. That moves AGT-1 and AGT-2 controls from prompt wording to policy.

top_opportunities.title: Publish @orca/process-host as a standalone package
top_opportunities.description: A 38-file package with no runtime npm dependencies, no Electron imports and a Node 18 floor that owns spawning, bounded output, cancellation, Windows .cmd shim and argument encoding, and process-tree termination with exit proof (src/packages/process-host/README.md:3; package.json engines '>=18', private, version 0.0.0). Other reviewed harnesses and installers (t3code, pandacode, caveman) spawn agent CLIs and face the same Windows quoting and orphan-process problems.

top_opportunities.title: Publish the typed-decision record as a versioned JSON Schema
top_opportunities.description: The answer object (choice/score/noul, probabilities, answer_confidence, abstention state and threshold, usage with truncation and collapsed options, routing) is consistent across the Python host, its ports and laya-coreml, but exists only in code and prose. A published schema lets REA/rex evidence records, strix-style coverage ledgers and agent harnesses (orca, t3code, pandacode, pi) consume decisions without reading prose, and lets contract drift fail CI.

top_opportunities.title: Calibrate rqs suggestions with rex's calibration
top_opportunities.description: rqs labels each suggestion observed, derived or inferred without measuring it (tools/rqs/rqs/suggest.py), and this review shows overconfident 'derived' levels. rex already records answers and adjudications and reports Wilson intervals, ECE and abstention advice (tools/rex/rex/epistemics.py:88-131). Recording each automatic level as a rex answer and adjudicating it with the reviewed level (a campaign of 15 reviews gives several hundred pairs) turns rqs's labels into measured precision per rule and lets weak rules abstain to U.

top_opportunities.title: Extract the egress layer as a reusable compose module
top_opportunities.description: The internal network plus allowlisting DNS and default-deny proxy is independent of the agent and could ship as a compose include or sidecar driven by one policy file. PandaCode's Full-access tasks, strix's sandboxed agents and t3code or orca harness runs could sit behind it.

top_opportunities.title: Keep 10.9 MB of images out of plugin installs
top_opportunities.description: The Claude Code marketplace source is the whole repository (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:13), so every plugin install carries 46 binaries totalling 10,929,610 bytes (localised banners and screenshots), while npm already excludes them (package.json:24-36).
